brief_summary: This prospective study will enroll 40 adults with clinically and histopathologically confirmed oral lichen planus to assess the association between oral vitamin C supplementation and outcomes of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT). All participants will receive five weekly ALA-PDT sessions and will be advised to take oral vitamin C at a dose of 1,000 mg once daily for five weeks, starting on the day of the first session. Participants will be compared according to their reported vitamin C use. The primary outcome will be the change in oral lesion surface area from baseline to one week after the final ALA-PDT session. Secondary outcomes will include changes in pain intensity measured using a 0-10 visual analog scale, clinical disease severity assessed using the reticular, erythematous, and ulcerative (REU) score, and salivary total antioxidant capacity (TAC) and total oxidant status (TOS).
primary_outcomes: Change in Oral Lichen Planus Lesion Surface Area
title: Vitamin C Supplementation and Photodynamic Therapy Outcomes in Oral Lichen Planus

brief_summary: The study will evaluate the effect of a Nurse-Led Digital STOP-PLAN-DO-REVIEW Parent Coaching Program on executive functioning, parenting stress, and behavioral problems among school-aged children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
primary_outcomes: Children whose parents receive the intervention will be assessed for executive-function difficulties compared with those receiving usual care.
Parenting stress will be assessed and compared between parents in the intervention group and those in the control group.
Behavioral and emotional difficulties will be assessed and compared between children in the intervention group and those in the control group.
title: Effect of a Nurse-Led Digital STOP-PLAN-DO-REVIEW Parent Coaching Program on Executive Function, Parenting Stress, and Behavioral Problems Among Children With ADHD

brief_summary: The goal of this study is to compare the bracket transfer accuracy of direct digital (DD) and indirect digital (ID) trays, which differ in manufacturing method, material, thickness and design. The main question it aims to answer is: Is there any differences in terms of bracket transfer accuracy between the two tray types? Pre- and post-bonding digital models are superimposed using local best-fit to measure linear (mesiodistal, vertical, buccolingual) and angular (tip, torque, rotation) transfer errors.
interventions: Bracket placement with direct digital (DD) bonding tray
Bracket placement with indirect digital (ID) bonding tray
primary_outcomes: The primary outcomes are the transfer errors.
title: Accuracy of Directly Versus Indirectly Fabricated Digital Indirect Bonding Trays

brief_summary: The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of multiple-dose HSK47388 versus placebo in participants with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants achieving PASI 90
Proportion of participants with an IGA score of 0 or 1 and a ≥2 point reduction from baseline
title: A Phase 3 Study of HSK47388 Tablets (I) to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety in Participants With Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psori

brief_summary: The calf muscle group (gastrocnemius and soleus) represents a strategic target in the management of lipedema, as it plays a central role in lymphatic drainage via the muscle pump mechanism and provides critical muscular strength for lower extremity functionality. To date, no studies in the existing literature have investigated the effects of isolated calf muscle strengthening exercises in patients with lipedema. Erdal et al. (2026) reported reduced muscle strength in patients with lipedema, further supporting the expectation of alterations in muscle architecture. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the effects of a progressive gastrocnemius and soleus muscle strengthening program, performed concurrently with aerobic exercise, on functionality, extremity circumference, muscle thickness/architecture, subcutaneous tissue thickness, pain, and quality of life in patients with lipedema.
interventions: Calf muscle strengthening exercises and aerobic exercise
primary_outcomes: Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS)
title: The Effect of Home-Based Calf Muscle Exercises on Lower Extremity Functionality and Muscle Architecture in Lipedema

brief_summary:
This interventional study aims to learn how atogepant, a medication approved to prevent migraines, affects migraine and body weight in adults who have both migraine and obesity.

The main questions are:

1. Is there a connection between starting atogepant and changes in migraine activity and body weight over time?
2. Do factors measured before starting atogepant help explain differences between people in how often they have migraines and how their weight changes, and how these two outcomes relate?
3. Do changing biological, behavioral, and psychological factors help explain how improvements in migraine relate to weight loss?

Participants will be followed for 44 weeks, with assessments at baseline, 12, 24, and 36 weeks. These assessments include 28 days of daily migraine activity tracking, daily weight measurements, behavioral monitoring, psychosocial questionnaires, biomarkers, and clinical/functional tests.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in migraine frequency over 40 weeks following initiation of atogepant treatment
Change from baseline in total body weight loss over 40 weeks following initiation of atogepant treatment
title: Longitudinal Investigation of Weight and Migraine With Atogepant in Clinical Obesity Settings

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to investigate whether an eight-week structured yoga program could improve mindfulness and emotional intelligence among undergraduate college students aged 18-23 years. The main questions it aimed to answer were:

* Does an eight-week yoga program improve mindfulness among college students compared with those who continue their usual daily activities?
* Does an eight-week yoga program improve emotional intelligence among college students compared with those who continue their usual daily activities?

Researchers compared students who participated in a structured yoga program with students who continued their usual academic and daily activities to determine whether regular yoga practice improved mindfulness and emotional intelligence.

A total of 80 undergraduate students were randomly assigned to two groups.

Participants in the yoga group:

* Attended supervised yoga sessions for 60 minutes per day, six days per week, for eight weeks.
* Practiced yoga postures (asanas), breathing exercises (pranayama), meditation, and relaxation.
* Completed questionnaires measuring mindfulness and emotional intelligence before and after the eight-week intervention.

Participants in the control group:

* Continued their usual academic and daily activities without participating in the structured yoga program.
* Completed the same mindfulness and emotional intelligence questionnaires at baseline and after eight weeks.

Mindfulness was measured using the 15-item Five-Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire (FFMQ-15), and emotional intelligence was assessed using the Mangal Emotional Intelligence Inventory (MEII).
primary_outcomes: Change in Mindfulness Score Assessed Using the Five-Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire (FFMQ-15)
Change in Emotional Intelligence Score Assessed Using the Mangal Emotional Intelligence Inventory (MEII)
title: Effect of an Eight-Week Yoga Program on Mindfulness and Emotional Intelligence in College Students

brief_summary:
Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels may increase after radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer, indicating a biochemical recurrence of the disease. Salvage radiotherapy is commonly used in this situation, but it may cause side effects that can affect patients' quality of life. For patients with a lower risk of disease progression and a negative PSMA PET scan, it is uncertain whether radiotherapy should be started early or whether it can be safely delayed.

This phase III randomized study will compare two management strategies in patients with low-risk biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy: early salvage radiotherapy initiated at a PSA level of 0.2 ng/mL or higher, and delayed salvage radiotherapy initiated at a PSA level of 0.5 ng/mL or higher. A total of 156 participants will be enrolled.

In addition to evaluating clinical outcomes, the study will assess healthcare costs and quality of life associated with both strategies. Quality of life will be measured using patient-reported outcomes, and healthcare resource utilization will be collected throughout the study and linked with national healthcare data sources. The study aims to determine whether delaying salvage radiotherapy can reduce treatment burden, improve quality of life, and optimize healthcare resource use while maintaining clinical outcomes comparable to those achieved with early radiotherapy.
primary_outcomes: Incremental Cost-Utility Ratio (ICUR) Expressed as Cost per Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY) Gained
title: Delayed Versus Early Salvage Radiotherapy for Low-Risk Biochemical Recurrence After Prostatectomy

brief_summary: This research study aims to learn if a home visiting program called +Language is Medicine can help caregivers learn and use skills to support young children's development. The investigators also want to know if the +Language is Medicine program improves children's development.
lead_sponsor: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health
primary_outcomes: Child Outcomes - Expressive Language as assessed by the Early Communication Indicator (ECI)
title: +Language is Medicine for Diné Toddlers

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Amimestrocel Injection in participants aged 14 years and older with steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD). Eligible participants will be randomized 1:1 to receive Amimestrocel Injection plus second-line therapy or placebo plus second-line therapy. Ruxolitinib is recommended as the preferred second-line therapy.

Confirmation of myeloid and platelet engraftment is required within 48 hours prior to initiation of study treatment: absolute neutrophil count (ANC) \> 1000/mm³ and platelets ≥ 20,000/mm³. Growth factor support and platelet transfusions are permitted.
lead_sponsor: Platinum Life Excellence Biotech Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: Overall response rate (ORR) at Day 28
title: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Amimestrocel Injection for Steroid-Refractory Acute Graft-versus-Host Disease (aGVHD)

brief_summary: This study employs a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, parallel-group, non-inferiority design. The trial will be conducted in virologically suppressed adult patients with HIV-1, using Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir Alafenamide (E/C/F/TAF) Tablets as the control, to demonstrate the efficacy and safety of the core investigational drug ACC007 combined with lamivudine (3TC) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) compared to E/C/F/TAF in treating virologically suppressed adult HIV-1 patients. After initial screening eligibility is confirmed, participants will return to the clinic on Day 1 (D1) for re-evaluation of eligibility and completion of required examinations. Eligible participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either ACC007/3TC/TDF Tablets (150/300/300 mg, once daily \[QD\]) or E/C/F/TAF Tablets (150/150/200/10 mg, QD). Both treatment groups will also receive matching placebos (double-dummy) and will undergo 48 weeks of continuous double-blind treatment. Subsequently, all study participants will transition to open-label treatment with ACC007/3TC/TDF for an additional 48 weeks (during which the dummy medication will no longer be administered).
lead_sponsor: Jiangsu Aidea Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with HIV-1 RNA ≥50 copies/mL at week 48、96、144、192、240
title: A Study of Switching to ACC007 Fixed-Dose Combination in Virologically-Suppressed Adults With HIV-1

brief_summary:
Papulopustular rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin condition that causes facial redness, papules, and pustules. This randomized clinical trial was designed to compare the effectiveness and safety of 2% tofacitinib ointment with 0.75% metronidazole gel in adults with moderate-to-severe papulopustular rosacea.

A total of 50 participants were randomly assigned to receive either 2% tofacitinib ointment or 0.75% metronidazole gel, applied twice daily for 12 weeks. Participants were then followed for an additional 12 weeks without treatment to assess whether improvements were maintained.

The study assessed disease severity, inflammatory lesion counts, quality of life, treatment-related adverse events, and recurrence of rosacea after treatment discontinuation.
lead_sponsor: Kurdistan Higher Council of Medical Specialties
primary_outcomes: Change in Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) Score
title: Comparative Efficacy of Topical Tofacitinib Versus Metronidazole in Papulopustular Rosacea

brief_summary: The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effect of peer-supported testicular self-examination (TSE) education on young men's health beliefs and TSE behavior. Testicular cancer is among the most common cancers in men aged 15-34, and regular TSE supports early detection, yet most young men do not perform it. A total of 128 men aged 18 and over living in a male student dormitory in Istanbul will be randomly assigned to an intervention group (n=64) that receives a 60-minute peer-led TSE education session, or a control group (n=64) that receives no intervention during the study. Health beliefs and TSE-related planned behavior will be measured at baseline and at 1 and 3 months.
primary_outcomes: Health Belief Scale for Testicular Cancer and Testicular Self-Examination subscale scores
Theory of Planned Behavior Scale related to Testicular Self-Examination scores
Testicular self-examination practice
title: Peer-Supported Testicular Self-Examination Education for Young Men

brief_summary: Transitioning from mechanical ventilation to extubation via the completion of a spontaneous breathing test (SBT) may not always be proven successful especially in patients of advanced age or underlying chronic cardiac or pulmonary conditions. Thus, by using electrical impedance tomography (EIT), which is non-invasive and radiation free, the researcher will identify changes in lung parameters when performing weaning to a mechanically ventillated patient and also post-extubation. This prospective observational psysiological study will include mechanically ventilated adults who are considered high risk for extubation failure and will undergo an SBT while performing an EIT assessment for a total of 65 minutes. Afterwards, monitoring will continue for 7 days in order to evaluate the patients' weaning outcome.
interventions: EIT-monitored non-invasive ventilation for weaning patients at high risk of extubation failure.
primary_outcomes: Difference in Respiratory Mechanics between succesful and failed weaning from a mechanical ventilator
title: Electrical Impedance Tomography in Weaning High Risk for Extubation Failure Patients.

brief_summary: This phase II trial tests the safety, side effects and best dose of abemaciclib in combination with radiation therapy and compares the effect of the combination to radiation therapy alone in treating patients with high-risk meningioma that is newly diagnosed or that has come back after a period of improvement (recurrent). Abemaciclib blocks certain proteins, which may help keep tumor cells from growing. It is a type of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor. Radiation therapy uses high energy x-rays, particles, or radioactive seeds to kill tumor cells and shrink tumors. Intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) is a type of 3-dimensional radiation therapy that uses computer-generated images to show the size and shape of the tumor. Thin beams of radiation of different intensities are aimed at the tumor from many angles. This type of radiation therapy reduces the damage to healthy tissues near the tumor. Pencil beam scanning (PBS) is a precise form of proton radiation therapy that uses an electronically guided scanning system and magnets to deliver a thin proton beam. This allows precise delivery of radiation to all three dimensions of the tumor. Giving abemaciclib in combination with radiation therapy may be safe and tolerable, and may be more effective than radiation therapy alone in preventing the tumor from growing or spreading in patients with newly diagnosed or recurrent high-risk meningioma.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of grade 3 or higher dose-limiting toxicities (Safety Lead-in)
Progression-free survival (PFS) (Randomized Phase II)
title: A Randomized Phase II Study of Radiation Therapy Alone Versus Radiation Therapy Plus Abemaciclib in Patients With High-Risk Meningioma, Including a Safety Lead-in Study

brief_summary: This study is evaluating the safety and feasibility of a potential new treatment for patients with progressive high-grade glioma. The treatment uses \[177Lu\]Lu-PSMA-I\&T, a radioactive drug that is administered directly into the blood vessels supplying the tumor. By delivering the treatment locally, researchers hope to increase radiation exposure to the tumor while limiting exposure to healthy tissues. Researchers aim to determine whether this novel radionuclide therapy can be administered safely and whether it shows signs of clinical benefit.
primary_outcomes: Maximum Tolerable Dose (MTD)
Phase 2 Recommended Dose (P2RD)
Objective Response Rate
title: A Phase 1-2 Study of Intra-arterial [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-I&T for Progressive High-grade Glioma

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Eucommia lignan liquid crystal cream works to improve crow's feet wrinkles in adults. It will also learn about the safety of this cream. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the cream reduce the severity of wrinkles on the outer corner of the eyes (crow's feet) compared to a blank cream without the active ingredient?

What medical problems or skin reactions do participants have when using the cream at different concentrations?

Researchers will compare three different concentrations of Eucommia lignan cream (0.5%, 1%, and 2%) to a blank cream (a look-alike substance that contains no Eucommia lignan) to see if the cream works and to explore the difference between doses. This is a split-face study, meaning each participant will use the active cream on one side of their face and the blank cream on the other side.

Participants will:

Apply the assigned active cream to one side of their face and the blank cream to the other side twice a day (morning and evening) for 8 weeks.

Visit the clinic at Week 4 and Week 8 for skin checkups, wrinkle assessments, and skin measurements.

Complete a follow-up visit about 2 weeks after stopping the cream to check for any delayed reactions.

Keep a diary of their daily product use, missed applications, and any skin reactions.
lead_sponsor: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change in Crow's Feet Wrinkle Score (VISIA) from Baseline to Week 8
title: A Split-Face, Double-Blind Study of Eucommia Lignan Cream for Crow' s Feet

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to develop and validate a telemetry system that measures the loads, movements, and oxygen levels of people taking part in human towers (castells), a traditional Catalan activity. It will include active castellers, mainly from the Castellers de Vilafranca group. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can the telemetry system record biomechanical and physiological data reliably, reproducibly, and safely during castell building?
* What loads do castellers bear on their shoulders, and how is weight distributed within the base (pinya) and the trunk of the tower?
* Do different base configurations, such as raising the arms in the pinya when the tower has a second base (folre), change the pressure within the core of the pinya?
* Do castellers in the core of the pinya have lower oxygen saturation than those in peripheral positions?

Participants will wear small non-invasive sensors (load cells, motion sensors, positioning tags, pulse oximeters, and heart rate monitors) during their usual rehearsals, and rehearsals will be video recorded. Participation does not change how they take part in the activity.
lead_sponsor: Consorci Sanitari de l'Alt Penedès i Garraf
primary_outcomes: Load on each shoulder
Trunk inclination
Spatial position of castellers
Load distribution within the "pinya"
Peripheral oxygen saturation
Vibration
title: Telemetry Monitoring of Loads, Movement, and Oxygen Saturation in Human Towers (Castells)
[Trial of device that is not approved or cleared by the U.S. FDA]

brief_summary: This study is testing a new retinal implant called the HARP4K Retinal Prosthesis System in people with severe vision loss caused by advanced retinal diseases, including age-related macular degeneration and retinitis pigmentosa. Up to five participants will receive the implant and be followed to assess its safety and how well it works. The main aim of the study is to determine whether the device and the implantation procedure can be used safely. The study will also explore whether the implant may help improve vision and quality of life. The information collected will help researchers decide whether the device should be evaluated in a larger future clinical study.
conditions: Geographic Atrophy Secondary to Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD-GA)
interventions: Subretinal implantation of HARP4K retinal prosthesis
primary_outcomes: Device and procedure safety related event
title: Early Feasibility Study of the HARP4K Retinal Prosthesis System in People With Advanced Retinal Degeneration.

brief_summary: This is a retrospective observational cohort study designed to characterize the natural history, treatment patterns, clinical outcomes, and healthcare resource utilization of adults living with obesity in the United Kingdom (UK). The study will provide real-world evidence on obesity and obesity management in routine clinical practice and support the design of four prospective cohorts intended to mirror the following three Phase 3 registrational, randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trials that are currently investigating the effects of ribupatide compared with placebo and semaglutide: K9531-3103 (NCT07284875), K9531-3104 (NCT07284901), and K9531-3107 (NCT07284979).
primary_outcomes: Percentage Change from Index Date in Body Weight at Week 76 Post-index Date
title: Impact of Novel GLP-1/GIP Medicines for Treating Obesity in the UK

brief_summary: The objective of this study is to examine the indications for the use of photochemotherapy in the context of kidney transplantation in France, as well as the outcomes regarding the renal graft and the patient (tolerability, survival).
primary_outcomes: Graft survival rate
title: Observatory of Extracorporeal Photochemotherapy in Kidney Transplantation

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out whether a food ingredient made from oyster mushroom and an algae called Chlorella helps with mild, everyday digestive discomfort, and whether it affects mood and cognitive function. We are testing three different amounts and comparing them to a placebo (a capsule with no study ingredient in it). You will not know if you receive the study ingredient or a placebo. The duration of this study is about 3 months. If you decide to participate, you will take capsules every morning for about 2 months, then stop taking them for 1 month while we check in with you. Everything happens at home. You will swallow 2 capsules every morning with liquid (e.g., water) for about 2 months. You will answer questionnaires about your digestion and your mood 4 times, play short brain games on a phone or computer 3 times, and answer a short check-in every 3 days. Some people will also be asked to collect 2 small stool (poop) samples at home and mail them back. This study is low risk. The capsules may cause mild bloating, cramping, gas, or changes in your bowel habits. Allergic reactions are rare but possible. Collecting a stool sample may be unpleasant. The questionnaires and brain games may make you tired or frustrated for a short time. You may or may not feel better from taking part. You may get the placebo.

What we learn may help people understand how this food ingredient affects digestive comfort and mood. You may or may not take part in this study. There is no cost to you. The capsules, any stool kits, and all shipping are provided by the sponsor. You can receive up to $100 for completing the study. There are provisions in place by the study protocol and the organising platform to help protect the privacy and confidentiality of your personal information and study data.
interventions: Co-fermentation food ingredient of Chlorella vulgaris microalgae and oyster mushroom mycelium (Pleurotus pulmonarius)
primary_outcomes: GSRS
title: TRIAL EVALUATING THE EFFICACY OF A FOOD INGREDIENT FROM OYSTER MUSHROOM MYCELIUM AND CHLORELLA MICROALGAE ON GASTROINTESTINAL SYMPTOMS, MOOD STATES, COGNITIVE FUNCTION AND STOOL BIOMARKERS IN HEALTHY ADULTS

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if orthodontic space closure with a miniscrew-anchored appliance (the mesialslider) works in patients with congenitally missing maxillary lateral incisors. It will also learn how the treatment affects patients' facial profile and daily lives. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does an active mesialslider move the upper first molars forward (mesialisation) during the first 6 months, compared with a passive mesialslider? How does mesialisation affect the 3D shape of the facial profile? How much pain and discomfort do participants experience, and how does the treatment affect their quality of life?

Researchers will compare an active mesialslider (activated immediately) to a passive mesialslider (a look-alike appliance where a metal sleeve prevents tooth movement for 6 months, after which it is activated) to see if the mesialslider works to close the space left by missing lateral incisors.

Participants will:

* Have two titanium mini-screws placed in the roof of the mouth under local anaesthesia, and the mesialslider will be attached to the upper first molars till they reach their desired position.
* Have 3D scans of their teeth and 3D photographs of their face taken before treatment, at the end of the first 6 months, and after treatment (control group: one additional scan after the active phase).
* Complete questionnaires about treatment motivation, pain, discomfort, use of pain medication, effects on daily activities, and quality of life (PIDAQ) at set time points, from the evening of screw insertion to one week after removal.
* Receive fixed braces for about 18 months after the mesialslider phase.
primary_outcomes: The primary outcome is the the movement of the first molar in the sagittal plane
title: Miniscrew Assisted Space Closure in Patients With Agenesis of an Upper Lateral Incisor. A Randomised Clinical Trial.

brief_summary: The project investigates the effects of non-invasive cervical trans-spinal direct current stimulation combined with rehabilitation therapy in patients with motor impairments caused by stroke or progressive multiple sclerosis. Its main objective is to determine whether this stimulation can amplify descending motor signals and increase spinal motoneuronal excitability to improve functional recovery of the upper limbs. The research evaluates these outcomes through clinical assessments, kinematic movement analysis, and the monitoring of blood biomarkers associated with neural plasticity and oxidative stress.
primary_outcomes: Functional improvement of 9-hole test
title: tsDCS for Neurological Patiens. A Clinical, Neurophysiological and Biomolecular Study.

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding an iliotibial band (ITB) graft to the standard repair of degenerative horizontal cleavage tears of the medial meniscus improves meniscal healing. The main question it aims to answer is: does ITB augmentation increase the rate of meniscal healing on MRI at 12 months compared with isolated meniscal repair? Participants with a degenerative horizontal cleavage tear of the medial meniscus will be randomly assigned during arthroscopy to either isolated arthroscopic meniscal repair or the same repair augmented with a strip of their own iliotibial band placed into the cleavage gap. Participants will attend follow-up visits at 6 weeks and 3, 6 and 12 months, complete knee questionnaires, and have a knee MRI at 12 months.
primary_outcomes: Meniscal healing on MRI
title: Iliotibial Band Augmentation in Medial Meniscus Horizontal Cleavage Tear Repair

brief_summary: This study examined whether structured counseling by midwives helps pregnant women take their multiple micronutrient supplement (MMS) every day. Nine primary health centers in Bone Bolango District, Gorontalo Province, Indonesia, were assigned, without randomization, to one of three approaches: individual interpersonal communication (four home visits by a trained midwife over 3 months, built around simple daily habits for taking the tablet, with follow-up through WhatsApp), group education in routine antenatal classes, or the standard information given when the supplement is dispensed. All women received the same MMS tablets through the national program. The study compared the number of tablets taken over 3 months, anemia at the end of that period, and delivery and newborn outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Adequate Multiple Micronutrient Supplement (MMS) Adherence
title: Midwife Counseling to Support Daily Multiple Micronutrient Supplement Use Among Pregnant Women in Gorontalo, Indonesia

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether rooming-in education delivered through a flipped classroom model improves psychosocial outcomes in couples expecting their first child. Participants are married couples with a singleton pregnancy at 24 weeks of gestation or later in which the pregnant partner is expecting her first child, recruited from the obstetric outpatient clinic of one hospital in Taoyuan, Taiwan.

The main question is whether, compared with traditional postpartum rooming-in education alone, adding prenatal flipped classroom education reduces anxiety in expectant mothers and fathers through the first 30 days after birth. The study also examines depressive symptoms, perceived social support, marital adjustment, and rooming-in rates in both groups, and learning satisfaction with the flipped classroom model in the intervention group.

The comparison group is enrolled first and receives traditional postpartum rooming-in education. The intervention group is enrolled after data collection in the comparison group is complete and receives the flipped classroom education during pregnancy in addition to the traditional postpartum education. Each partner completes questionnaires separately at enrollment and at 3, 10, and 30 days after birth.
lead_sponsor: National Taipei University of Nursing and Health Sciences
primary_outcomes: Anxiety symptoms
title: Flipped Classroom Rooming-in Education for Expectant Couples

brief_summary:
Periodontal pockets and infected root canals provide an anaerobic environment with similar nutrients that allows the migration of bacteria and their inflammatory byproducts through different anatomical communication pathways. This pathological communication between the pulp and periodontal tissues is defined as an endoperiodontal lesion (EPL) and multidisciplinary treatment (endodontic-periodontal) is required to achieve changes in the composition of the subgingival biofilm and generate a biologically suitable surface for the healing of periodontal tissues.

With the aim to evaluate the clinical and microbiological outcomes obtained after performing the endodontic treatment and subgingival instrumentation, a randomized clinical trial was designed using a Sodium hypochlorite gel in the test group.

Methods and analysis:

36 patients with a diagnosis of periodontitis and at least one endoperiodontal lesion, who begin their treatment at the Faculty of Dentistry of the University of Buenos Aires (FOUBA), will be included in a triple-blind randomized clinical trial. After randomization, endodontic treatment and subgingival instrumentation (using a Sodium hypochlorite gel as adjuvant in the test group) will be performed. After 30 days, reduction in probing depth (PD), clinical attachment level (CAL) gain, presence of residual pockets \> 4mm and bacterial count is going to be evaluated and the results published in a peer-reviewed journal.
primary_outcomes: Probing Depth
title: Treatment of Endoperiodontal Lesion Using a Sodium Hypoclorite Gel as Adjuvant.

brief_summary:
This study will look at whether bedside stomach ultrasound can help guide tube feeding in adults who need a breathing machine in the intensive care unit.

In the first stage, researchers will use ultrasound to measure the size of part of the stomach at several time points during routine tube feeding. They will use these measurements and information on how well patients tolerate feeding to develop a tool that helps guide changes in the feeding rate.

In the second stage, researchers will compare feeding guided by this tool with usual feeding care. They will look at how well patients tolerate tube feeding and whether they reach their planned feeding rate.
conditions: Enteral Feeding Tolerance in Critically Ill Patients
primary_outcomes: Gastric Antral Cross-Sectional Area
title: Dynamic Optimization of Enteral Nutrition Using Gastric Ultrasound in Mechanically Ventilated Critically Ill Patients

brief_summary: The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the effects of virtual reality (VR)-based education and face-to-face education on self-care behaviors in adults with type 2 diabetes. Participants are randomly assigned to receive either an interactive VR education session delivered through a VR headset or a face-to-face education session with the same content. Both sessions last about 20 minutes and cover hyperglycemia, hypoglycemia, chronic complications, and preventive self-care (foot care). Self-care is measured with the Diabetes Self-Care Scale before the education and four weeks after it. The study also examines whether VR education is feasible and safe for this population.
primary_outcomes: Change in Diabetes Self-Care Scale (DSCS) total score
title: Virtual Reality Versus Face-to-Face Education for Self-Care in Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary: This cross-sectional study aims to measure fetal biometric parameters using automated and manual methods on obstetric ultrasound.
primary_outcomes: Biparietal diameter
title: Automated Fetal Biometric Measurements in Obstetric Ultrasound

brief_summary: HEBest is a prospective, non-interventional German patient registry for adults with moderate-to-severe chronic hand eczema who are initiating treatment recommended for use in routine clinical care. Treatment decisions are made jointly by the treating dermatologist and patient.The registry does not assign or modify treatment. It collects physician-reported clinical data and patient-reported outcomes through electronic case report forms and questionnaires. The registry aims to describe treatment patterns, disease severity and course, treatment response, health-related quality of life, patient-reported treatment benefit, and safety in routine dermatological care.
primary_outcomes: Hand Eczema Severity Index(HECSI)
Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI)
title: German Chronic Hand Eczema Registry

brief_summary: This randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial compares the analgesic effects of intra-articular ketamine, intra-articular ketorolac, and normal saline following elective knee arthroscopy under spinal anesthesia in adult patients. The study evaluates postoperative pain scores, time to first rescue analgesic request, and total morphine consumption during the first 24 postoperative hours.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative pain scores at rest
title: Intra-Articular Ketamine Versus Ketorolac for Analgesia After Knee Arthroscopy

brief_summary: The goal of this study is to test the feasibility of a wearable sleeve device. For patients with OCD who enroll in this study, ERP (exposure and response prevention) therapy will be provided through the study, free of charge. The sleeve is a MXene and silicone device worn on the forearm which measures muscle activity, heart rate, arm position, and other physiological markers. Our hope is that the data collected by the sleeve will correlate with psychiatric scales collected by our clinical psychology team, which will enable us to measure these conditions using the sleeve alone.
primary_outcomes: Duration of wearing sleeve
title: Smart Sleeve for Psychiatric Conditions (OCD, and Others)

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to examine the effect of an 8-week, face-to-face, group-based Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) psychoeducation program on gaming severity, psychological flexibility, emotion regulation, and perceived stress in university students aged 18 to 25 who show high-risk internet gaming behavior. The program is delivered by a psychiatric nurse.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does ACT-based psychoeducation reduce internet gaming severity?
* Does ACT-based psychoeducation increase psychological flexibility?
* Does ACT-based psychoeducation reduce emotion regulation difficulties?
* Does ACT-based psychoeducation reduce perceived stress?

Researchers will compare the ACT group with a waitlist control group that receives no intervention until the 3-month follow-up is completed.

Participants will:

* Complete an online screening questionnaire in the fall semester
* If eligible, complete online questionnaires at the start of the spring semester (baseline), after the program (week 8), and 3 months later
* If assigned to the ACT group, attend 8 weekly group sessions of 45 to 60 minutes

Students in the waitlist group will be offered the same program after data collection ends.
primary_outcomes: Change in Internet Gaming Disorder Scale-Short Form (IGDS9-SF) Score
title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-Based Psychoeducation for University Students With High-Risk Internet Gaming Behavior

brief_summary:
This prospective, observational, analytical, controlled cross-sectional study aims to investigate the relationship between subcutaneous tissue stiffness measured by shear wave elastography (SWE), pain phenotype, and functional impairment in women with lipedema.

A total of 100 women aged 18-65 years will be enrolled, including 50 patients with clinically diagnosed lipedema and 50 body mass index (BMI)-matched obese controls without lipedema.

Participants will undergo ultrasonographic and SWE assessments, pain evaluation, functional assessments, and quality-of-life measurements. The study aims to determine the clinical significance of SWE findings in lipedema.
primary_outcomes: Subcutaneous Tissue Stiffness Measured by Shear Wave Elastography
title: Clinical Significance of Shear Wave Elastography in Women With Lipedema

brief_summary:
Ankle sprains are very common in youth soccer and can lead to ongoing ankle weakness and instability, known as chronic ankle instability (CAI). This condition makes it harder for players to move quickly and increases their risk of getting injured again. Balance exercises (proprioceptive training) are often used to help players recover, but it is unclear whether doing these exercises on flat, stable ground or on unstable surfaces (like balance pads or wobble boards) works better.

The goal of this study was to compare the effects of a 6-week balance training program on a stable surface versus an unstable surface in youth male soccer players with CAI. Thirty-three players (average age 17 years) were randomly placed into one of three groups:

* A group doing balance exercises on a stable surface (11 players)
* A group doing the same exercises on an unstable surface (11 players)
* A control group continuing their normal soccer training without extra balance exercises (11 players) Before and after the 6-week program, researchers measured the players' dynamic balance (using the Y-Balance Test) and change-of-direction speed (using the Illinois Agility Test). The results showed that players who trained on a stable surface improved their balance and agility the most, followed by those who trained on an unstable surface.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Dynamic Balance Assessed by the Y-Balance Test (YBT) Composite Score at 6 Weeks
Change from Baseline in Change-of-Direction Speed Assessed by the Illinois Agility Test at 6 Weeks
title: Stable vs. Unstable Surface Proprioceptive Training for Balance and Agility in Youth Soccer Players With Ankle Instability.

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate the effects of mechanical knee traction combined with conventional physical therapy compared with conventional physical therapy alone on pain, disability, proprioception, balance, and musculoskeletal properties in patients with knee osteoarthritis.

Thirty-eight participants aged 45 to 65 years with knee osteoarthritis will be randomly assigned to either an experimental group receiving mechanical knee traction combined with conventional physical therapy or a control group receiving conventional physical therapy alone.

Both groups will receive treatment three times per week for four weeks. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at a four-week follow-up to evaluate the additional effects of mechanical knee traction.
primary_outcomes: Change in Knee Pain Intensity Measured by the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: The Impact of Mechanical Knee Traction Combined With Conventional Physical Therapy on Pain, Disability, Sensorimotor Function and Musculoskeletal Properties in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this three-arm randomised controlled trial is to learn if a large-language-model-driven CBT journalling supporter (LEO) can reduce procrastination among young adults (18 to 24 years) with General Procrastination Scale scores over 59. The specific aims of the research include:

1. Assess the feasibility and acceptability of LEO for addressing procrastination among young adults in Hong Kong, including adherence, engagement, and user satisfaction.
2. Evaluate LEO's effectiveness in supporting CBT-informed journalling, focusing on usability, frequency and completeness of entries, and the quality of reflective content.
3. Evaluate the preliminary effectiveness of LEO in reducing procrastination and improving mental well-being and functional outcomes, relative to control and active control conditions.
interventions: CBT journalling with an LLM-driven supporter (LEO)
CBT journalling on a web-based platform
primary_outcomes: General Procrastination Scale (GPS)
title: Project LEO (Learn-Execute-Overcome): An LLM-driven CBT Journalling Supporter to Reduce Procrastination Among Young Adults

brief_summary: Pilot feasibility and acceptability study, using a prospective, descriptive, mixed-methods, multicentre design, conducted in four Home Care Services in the region. Five social and healthcare support workers will be recruited at each centre to visit older adults in their homes, measure their weight, assess their food intake and implement the malnutrition screening protocol.
conditions: Education on Feeding and Health Status
primary_outcomes: Rate of fully compliant malnutrition screening protocols for older adults over 6 months
title: Clinical Screening for Undernutrition in the Elderly Person With Loss of Autonomy : a Feasibility and Acceptability Syudy

brief_summary: The study aimed to assess the reliability of lung ultrasound score (LUS) in predicting weaning outcomes and to identify the main causes of weaning failure in critically ill mechanically ventilated patients.
primary_outcomes: assess weaning patterns either successful or failed weaning using lung ultrasound
title: LUS for Weaning Prediction in RICU

brief_summary: This prospective, multicenter, phase IV study investigates the role of ctDNA as biomarker for guiding the prognosis of mUC patients during first-line therapy with enfortumab vedotin (EV) +pembrolizumab. A de-intensification strategy (EV interruption and pembrolizumab maintenance) in patients with ctDNA clearance will decrease the rate of side effects related to treatment, without compromising patients' survival outcomes. This will provide a revolutionary molecular-based rational able to drive management decision and optimization of first-line treatment for metastatic urothelial carcinoma patients, optimizing the efficacy while limiting toxicity and preserving the quality of life.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione Policlinico Universitario Agostino Gemelli IRCCS
primary_outcomes: 1-Year Progression-Free Survival (PFS) Rate by ctDNA Clearance Status
title: ctDNA-guided Enfortumab Vedotin Plus Pembrolizumab in Untreated Patients With Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma

brief_summary: This four-center randomized trial compares two mobile exercise prescription policies in preservice teachers in Uzbekistan. Both groups use the same OptiForma application and exercise library for 16 weeks, with three nonconsecutive sessions per week. In the adaptive arm, prescribed active time is modified using rules based on completion, perceived exertion, symptoms and current fatigue. In the fixed arm, the initial prescription is retained, with the same safety reductions when required. The primary outcome is the number of fully completed 20-m shuttle-run segments at week 16. Physical fitness tests, practicum fatigue, adherence and harms are assessed separately. Follow-up continues through week 28.
primary_outcomes: Number of fully completed 20-m shuttle-run segments
title: Adaptive Versus Fixed Mobile Exercise in Preservice Teachers

brief_summary: The Tame-LC trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIb trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of semaglutide administered subcutaneously once-weekly for improvement of overall Health-related Quality of Life (HRQoL) and select symptoms in adolescents and adults aged 12 to 70 years with Long COVID. A total of 774 participants (642 adults and 132 adolescents) will be randomized in a 2:2:1:1 allocation ratio to receive semaglutide up to 1.0 mg (maximum tolerated dose), semaglutide up to 2.4 mg (maximum tolerated dose), placebo up to 1.0 mg, or placebo up to 2.4 mg. The trial involves a combination of patient-reported outcomes (PROs), other assessments (e.g., cognitive tests, 6-minute walk test), and blood biomarkers that may be useful for tracking improvement (e.g., inflammatory, immunologic, neurologic, cardiovascular, and metabolic biomarkers. Semaglutide is expected to provide clinical benefits to a wide array of symptoms regardless of weight loss. Therefore, the study will evaluate improvements in HRQoL but also specific clinical features of Long COVID, including fatigue, cognitive difficulties, dysautonomia, and post-exertional malaise (PEM), in treatment versus placebo arms. In addition, it will evaluate the specific doses at which benefits are observed via randomization of participants to one of two dosing arms. Durability of improvement will be evaluated 3 months after cessation of study product. The primary objective is to evaluate the effect of a 6-month course of semaglutide compared to placebo on the change in overall HRQoL from baseline to 6 months after randomization among participants aged 18-70 years with Long COVID.
lead_sponsor: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
primary_outcomes: Change in the PROMIS (Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System)-29+2 PROPr (PROMIS-Preference) score among participants aged 18-70 years with Long COVID
title: RECOVER-TLC Semaglutide Treatment Trial

brief_summary: This pilot study examines whether the negative emotion(s) triggered by the memory of a traumatic event disappear during a single session of ViEtRis®, a brief method combining hypnosis, conscious work and bilateral tapping, and whether they remain absent one month later. Participants do not have to recount the traumatic event. Emotional intensity is rated from 0 to 10 at booking, at the start and end of the session, and one month later. Post-traumatic symptoms are also measured with the International Trauma Questionnaire (ITQ). A waiting period of 2 to 4 weeks before the session checks whether emotions decrease on their own.
primary_outcomes: Emotional intensity linked to the traumatic memory (Subjective Units of Distress, 0 to 10)
title: Single-Session ViEtRis® Method for the Emotional Charge of Traumatic Memories: a Pilot Study

brief_summary: The proposed translational research will address greater rates of overdose, suicide ideation and behaviors, substance use and mental health problems and the substantial unmet treatment need among young adults involved in the criminal legal system (YACL). The investigators will capitalize on an established, nationwide, evidence-based employment training program (Center for Employment Opportunities; CEO) and leverage existing local peer recovery support services to screen/ identify, refer, and engage YACL in substance use and mental health treatment, including medications for opioid use disorder and stimulant, treatment, via e-ConnectYA and to identify implementation strategies that support this multi-level, cross-system approach to treatment linkage. Guided by the Gateway Provider Model (GPM) and Exploration Preparation Implementation and Sustainment (EPIS) frameworks, this 5-year study will first tailor e-Connect -- our efficacious system-level intervention designed to improve identification of suicide risk, substance use and mental health problems, increase referrals and increase treatment uptake for adolescents on probation -- to accommodate the needs of YACL by including overdose risk screening and integrating local peer supportive services to create e-ConnectYA. Investigators will then use a type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation stepped-wedge trial design in CEO sites across 6 states (CA, KY, NC, OH, OK, PA) to examine the effectiveness of e-ConnectYA.
primary_outcomes: substance use/mental health treatment initiation
title: Engaging Criminal Legal System-involved Young Adults Through Supportive Employment

brief_summary:
This prospective comparative cohort study aims to compare the clinical outcomes and safety of Yamane sutureless scleral-fixated intraocular lens implantation versus retropupillary iris-claw intraocular lens implantation in patients with aphakia and inadequate capsular support.

The study will include 96 patients divided into two groups of 48 patients each. The first group will undergo retropupillary iris-claw IOL implantation at Alforsan Eye Center, Assiut, while the second group will undergo Yamane flanged intrascleral IOL fixation at Watany Eye Hospitals, Cairo.

All patients will undergo preoperative ophthalmic assessment and postoperative follow-up for 12 months. The primary outcome will be IOL positional stability, assessed by measuring IOL tilt and decentration using anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT). Secondary outcomes will include visual and refractive outcomes, endothelial cell density, intraocular pressure, reoperation rates, and intraoperative and postoperative complications.
primary_outcomes: Intraocular Lens (IOL) Tilt
Intraocular Lens (IOL) Decentration
title: Yamane Versus Retropupillary Iris-Claw IOL Implantation in Aphakia

brief_summary:
* This study will examine whether showing predicted consequences alongside an artificial intelligence (AI) treatment recommendation affects physicians' decisions about intravenous fluids and vasopressors for patients with sepsis. The AI system compares the current treatment plan with alternatives and predicts how the patient's condition may change under each plan. It may recommend a change when the predicted benefit is consistent across several plausible assumptions; otherwise, it states that the evidence is insufficient to recommend a change.
* About 72 physicians from two hospitals will review 30 retrospective, de-identified intensive care decision points. In the first stage, each physician will make treatment decisions without AI information. In the second stage, physicians will review cases under three conditions: the case with the on-duty clinician's plan but no AI information (B0); the same information plus an AI recommendation (B1); and the same recommendation plus predicted consequences for the current and recommended plans (B2). The conditions will be assigned across case blocks using counterbalanced sequences. Physicians will be stratified by clinical seniority, without specifying years of experience.
* Final decisions will be compared with treatment plans independently made by an expert panel. The study will estimate differences in decision quality across conditions; the direction and size of any differences are unknown. No patients will be enrolled or treated, and physicians' study decisions will not affect patient care.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Acceptable Treatment Decisions
title: Reliability Information and Physicians' Treatment Decisions in Sepsis With Respiratory Failure

brief_summary:
The overall objective of the study is to characterize in depth a series of ALS patients and at-risk family members to obtain an overview of the pathophysiology of the disease from its presymptomatic stages to more advanced stages. The aim is to identify new biomarkers, open up new therapeutic avenues, and promote the application of precision medicine. Specifically, the role played by genetics, microbiota, and metabolic and epigenetic changes in the development and progression of the disease will be analyzed.

To this end, three cohorts will be studied longitudinally: 100 ALS patients (including 20 with C9ORF72 expansions), 40 presymptomatic carriers of C9ORF72 expansions, and 40 controls (family members who are not mutation carriers). In all of them, motor and cognitive impairment will be characterized in depth and the following biomarkers will be analyzed: i) Neurodegeneration: serum light neurofilament; ii) Metabolism: various targeted metabolites, bioimpedance, calorimetry, fasciculations, and subcutaneous and visceral fat measured by ultrasound.

This evaluation will be repeated at 6 months in patients and at 2 years in presymptomatic carriers.

In a subgroup of 40 sporadic patients, 20 C9ORF72, 20 presymptomatic C9ORF72 carriers, and 40 controls, the following will also be performed upon recruitment, metagenomic studies in stool, untargeted lipidomics in plasma and feces, and a targeted study of genes of interest in metabolism and ALS and DNA methylation using long-read sequencing technology in blood.

Throughout the study, participants will be clinically monitored according to standard clinical practice, using survival (patients) and disease onset (carriers) as primary endpoints.

At the end of the study, the relationship between the biomarkers and microbiota analyzed will be analyzed in relation to disease progression.
primary_outcomes: Overall survival in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)
Occurrence of clinically manifest ALS in presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers
title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), a Complex Interaction of Genes, Metabolism, and Environment: Precision Medicine Applied to ALS

brief_summary: Evidence regarding the effectiveness of Direct Observation of Procedural Skills (DOPS) during real clinical knee arthroscopy remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The objective of the present study is to evaluate the effectiveness of DOPS in improving diagnostic knee arthroscopy skills among postgraduate orthopedic trainees by comparing procedural skill scores before and after the intervention.
interventions: Individualized Formative Feedback Based on DOPS Assessment
primary_outcomes: Change in Diagnostic Knee Arthroscopy Procedural Skill Scores
title: Effectiveness of Direct Observation of Procedural Skills (DOPS) for Improving the Diagnostic Knee Arthroscopy Skills

brief_summary:
Acute heart failure is a serious condition associated with high risks of worsening heart failure, rehospitalization, and death. Inflammation may contribute to disease progression in some patients with acute heart failure, and short-term corticosteroid treatment may help reduce inflammation and improve clinical outcomes.

This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study will evaluate whether a short course of prednisone acetate, when added to standard treatment, improves outcomes in hospitalized adults with acute heart failure and elevated inflammatory markers. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either prednisone acetate 40 mg once daily or matching placebo for 14 days, in addition to standard treatment for acute heart failure. Participants will be followed for 90 days.

The study will assess the effects of prednisone treatment on mortality, worsening heart failure, health-related quality of life, congestion, and other clinical and laboratory outcomes, as well as treatment safety.
primary_outcomes: Hierarchical Composite Endpoint of All-Cause Death, Worsening Heart Failure, change from baseline in EQ-VAS, and change from baseline in Congestion Score
title: Prednisone for Acute Heart Failure With Elevated Inflammatory Markers

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to examine the relationship between walking performance, cognitive function, and freezing of gait (FOG) in people with Parkinson's disease and healthy control participants. FOG is a temporary inability to start or continue walking, even when a person wants to move. The study will use the Trail-Walking Test (TWT), which assesses walking while completing a task that requires attention and thinking.

The main questions are:

How is TWT performance related to cognitive function?

Does TWT performance differ between people with Parkinson's disease and healthy control participants?

Among people with Parkinson's disease, is TWT performance related to the presence or severity of FOG?

Participants will complete the TWT and cognitive assessments. Researchers will also collect information about walking difficulties and FOG. The researchers will compare results between people with Parkinson's disease and healthy control participants and examine relationships between walking performance, cognitive function, and FOG. The findings may help researchers better understand these relationships and support future research into ways to assess walking and cognitive difficulties in Parkinson's disease.
conditions: Freezing of Gait Symptoms in Parkinson Disease
primary_outcomes: TWT's relation to cognitive function beyond gait
title: Relationship Between Cognitive Function, Trail-Walking Test Performance, and Freezing of Gait in Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the effects of laryngeal rehabilitation (laryngeal manual therapy) and voice therapy on voice parameters in adults aged 18 to 50 with primary muscle tension dysphonia.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How do laryngeal rehabilitation and voice therapy change acoustic voice quality (Acoustic Voice Quality Index, AVQI)?
* How do the two treatments affect voice efficiency (maximum phonation time, s/z ratio, phonation quotient), voice handicap, neck awareness, pain, and neck pain-related disability?

Researchers will compare a laryngeal rehabilitation group with a voice therapy group.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two groups
* Receive treatment 2 days per week for 6 weeks
* In the laryngeal rehabilitation group, receive kneading of the sternocleidomastoid, suprahyoid and laryngeal regions followed by laryngeal depression (lowering) manoeuvres
* In the voice therapy group, receive 45-minute structured voice therapy sessions (diaphragmatic breathing, straw phonation, resonant voice therapy and Vocal Function Exercises)
* Complete acoustic voice recordings, voice efficiency measurements and questionnaires before and after treatment
primary_outcomes: Change in Acoustic Voice Quality Index (AVQI)
title: Laryngeal Rehabilitation Versus Voice Therapy in Muscle Tension Dysphonia

brief_summary:
Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder that frequently affects adolescents and may be associated with compulsive exercise and difficulties regulating physical activity. Although physical activity may have potential benefits when appropriately adapted and medically supervised, its role in the treatment of AN remains insufficiently investigated.

The BALANCE study aims to evaluate the effects of adding a structured adapted physical activity programme (PAPAPAM) to treatment as usual (TAU) in adolescents aged 12-17 years with AN. The study will also explore whether adding a cognitive-behavioural intervention targeting compulsive exercise (LEAP) provides additional benefits in participants presenting motor restlessness.

Participants will be stratified according to the presence or absence of motor restlessness and randomly allocated to treatment conditions. Participants without motor restlessness will receive either TAU alone or TAU plus PAPAPAM. Participants presenting motor restlessness will be allocated to TAU alone, TAU plus PAPAPAM, or TAU plus PAPAPAM and LEAP.

PAPAPAM and LEAP will each consist of eight weekly sessions delivered by trained professionals. All participants will continue to receive their usual multidisciplinary treatment.

The primary outcome is the change in clinician-rated global clinical severity, assessed using the Clinical Global Impression-Severity (CGI-S) scale, from baseline to the end of the eight-week intervention.

Secondary outcomes include global functioning, compulsive exercise, eating-disorder psychopathology, body image, nutritional status, physical functioning, and health-related quality of life. The feasibility, acceptability, and safety of the interventions will also be evaluated.

The study is expected to provide preliminary evidence on the integration of adapted physical activity into the multidisciplinary treatment of adolescents with AN.
lead_sponsor: IRCCS National Neurological Institute "C. Mondino" Foundation
primary_outcomes: Change in Clinical Global Impression-Severity (CGI-S) Score from Baseline to Week 8
title: Body Awareness and Lived Activity in Nutrition-Related Conditions and Exercise Behaviours in Adolescents With Anorexia Nervosa

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to establish a cefuroxime population pharmacokinetic model applicable to elderly patients undergoing gynecological surgery, explore the effects of age, body weight, renal function, and surgical type on the in vivo process of cefuroxime, evaluate the probability of target attainment of conventional clinical doses through PK/PD Monte Carlo simulation, and optimize individualized perioperative prophylactic medication regimens for this specific elderly population in elderly female patients undergoing gynecological surgery. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can a reliable population pharmacokinetic model of cefuroxime be established for elderly patients undergoing gynecological surgery? How do key covariates including age, body weight, renal function and surgical type affect the pharmacokinetic characteristics of cefuroxime in elderly gynecological surgical patients? Can conventional cefuroxime doses achieve satisfactory antibacterial target attainment in elderly gynecological surgical patients, and what are the risks of insufficient drug exposure or drug accumulation? Can optimized individualized prophylactic medication regimens improve the safety and efficacy of perioperative anti-infection prophylaxis in elderly gynecological surgery patients?
primary_outcomes: Cefuroxime concentration

CV%
title: Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis and Dose Optimization of Cefuroxime for Perioperative Prophylaxis in Elderly Gynecological Surgery Patients

brief_summary:
Title: Parent-administered Pediatric Tuina Versus Behavioral Sleep Intervention in Improving Sleep Disturbance among Children with Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Non-inferiority Randomized Controlled Trial with Mixed-method Process Evaluation

Background: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects a significant proportion of children worldwide, with sleep disturbances being a prevalent and challenging comorbidity. Existing treatments for sleep problems in children with ADHD primarily include pharmacological approaches and behavioral sleep intervention (BSI), both of which have limitations such as side effects, behavioral demands, and accessibility issues. Parent-administered pediatric tuina (PPT), a non-pharmacological manual therapy rooted in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), offers a potentially effective, safe, and accessible alternative to improve sleep disturbances and related ADHD symptoms. Preliminary studies have demonstrated the feasibility and promising effects of PPT in ADHD families in Hong Kong and mainland China.

Objective: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of a standardized PPT protocol compared with BSI and waitlist control in improving sleep disturbance among children aged 4 to 8 years with ADHD. Additionally, the study includes a mixed-methods process evaluation to explore facilitators, barriers, and the specific effects of PPT beyond shared therapeutic components.

Methods: This three-arm, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial (RCT) includes an embedded mixed-methods process evaluation. A total of 270 parent-child dyads (children aged 4-8 years with ADHD) will be stratified by age (4-6 and 6-8 years) and randomized 1:1:1 to PPT, BSI, or waitlist groups. The PPT group parents will attend two 1-hour training sessions by TCM practitioners, covering theory and practical skills for a standardized five-acupoint protocol, with competency assessment required. Parents will perform 30-minute sessions every two days for 8 weeks at home, monitored via logbooks and bi-weekly reminders. The BSI group will receive eight weekly 120-minute psychoeducation sessions by clinical psychologists, covering sleep hygiene, behavioral management, and communication techniques, with between-session exercises and adherence logging. Waitlist controls will receive intervention materials post-study. Primary outcome is sleep disturbance (Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children) assessed at baseline, weeks 4, 8, and 12. Secondary outcomes include ADHD symptoms (Conners Parent Rating Scale-Revised), quality of life (PedsQL), parenting stress (PSI-SF), and actigraphy sleep parameters at baseline and week 12. Process evaluation combines quantitative assessments of acceptability, adherence, feasibility, and safety through post-training quizzes, logbooks, and adverse event monitoring, with qualitative data from post-intervention focus group interviews analyzed using thematic analysis. Cost-effectiveness analysis will assess intervention, direct medical, and non-medical costs from healthcare provider perspective, calculating incremental cost-effectiveness ratios with uncertainty evaluated through bootstrapping and acceptability curves. Data analysis will employ linear mixed-effects models for primary and secondary outcomes under intention-to-treat principle, with multiple imputation for missing data. Qualitative analysis will identify implementation facilitators and barriers through thematic analysis.
primary_outcomes: Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC) Chinese version
title: Parent-administered Pediatric Tuina Versus Behavioral Sleep Intervention for Sleep Disturbance in Children With ADHD

brief_summary: The main objective of this trial is to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of a single subcutaneous dose of ION573 alone, and ION573 coadministered with ION775 as separate single doses.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)
title: A Trial to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of ION573 With and Without ION775

brief_summary: This pilot study will explore pain relief, functional improvement, safety, and feasibility of transforaminal epidural polydeoxyribonucleotide (PDRN) injections in adults with chronic lumbosacral radicular pain caused by lumbar disc herniation. Thirty participants will be randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to repeated PDRN injections or a steroid-based comparison regimen. Participants and outcome evaluators will be blinded. The main comparison is the percentage reduction in pain score four weeks after the final procedure.
primary_outcomes: Percentage Reduction in Radicular Pain NRS at V4
title: Transforaminal Epidural PDRN Versus Steroid for Chronic Lumbosacral Radicular Pain

Participants will be randomly assigned to either an intervention group receiving the gamification-based digital program or a control group receiving standard care. Outcomes will be assessed using validated scales to determine the effectiveness of the digital intervention in improving patient self-management and overall well-being.

brief_summary:
Title: Cosmetic and Functional Outcomes of Congenital Ptosis Surgery. This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the cosmetic and functional outcomes of congenital ptosis surgery in children.

Approximately 40-50 children undergoing levator surgery or frontalis sling will be included.

Preoperative assessment will include MRD1, levator function, ptosis severity, and visual axis evaluation.

Patients will be followed up for six months to assess eyelid position, symmetry, functional improvement, and postoperative complications.

The study will help evaluate surgical outcomes and identify factors associated with successful correction of congenital ptosis.
primary_outcomes: Change in Margin Reflex Distance 1 (MRD1)
Postoperative eyelid symmetry (measured by Margin Reflex Distance 1 "MRD1")
title: Study of Cosmetic and Functional Outcome of Congenital Ptosis Surgery at Sohag University

brief_summary: This study aims to explore whether the lung ultrasound score (LUS) can predict treatment failure of ibuprofen for patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in preterm infants. The investigators will retrospectively collect clinical data of preterm infants receiving ibuprofen for PDA, analyze the relationship between LUS and treatment outcomes, and identify the predictive value of LUS for ibuprofen treatment failure. This is a single-center retrospective observational study.
conditions: Patent Ductus Arteriosus in Preterm Infants
primary_outcomes: Rate of ibuprofen treatment failure for hsPDA

This is a prospective, open-label, single-arm, non-randomized, exploratory clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy of liposomal irinotecan (II) combined with 5-fluorouracil/leucovorin (5-FU/LV) and cetuximab beta as first-line treatment for patients with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC).

Approximately 35 patients aged 18 to 75 years with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer and RAS/BRAF wild-type tumors will be enrolled.

The study consists of two stages: a safety run-in stage and a preliminary efficacy evaluation stage.

During the safety run-in stage, 3 to 6 patients will initially receive combination therapy with liposomal irinotecan (II) at 60 mg/m². Dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) will be assessed during the first 14 days. If the initial dose is not tolerated, a reduced dose of 50 mg/m² will be evaluated. The recommended phase II dose (RP2D) will be determined based on safety, tolerability, and preliminary antitumor activity. Pharmacokinetic assessments of liposomal irinotecan (II) and cetuximab beta will also be performed.

During the preliminary efficacy evaluation stage, patients will receive liposomal irinotecan (II) at the RP2D in combination with cetuximab beta and 5-FU/LV every two weeks. The primary efficacy endpoint is the objective response rate (ORR) at 24 weeks, assessed according to RECIST version 1.1.

Secondary efficacy endpoints include time to response (TTR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and quality of life. Safety will be evaluated by monitoring adverse events according to NCI-CTCAE version 5.0.

Tumor assessments will be performed every 8 weeks during treatment, and survival follow-up will be conducted every 3 months after treatment discontinuation.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Treatment-Related Adverse Events (TRAEs) and Dose-Limiting Toxicities (DLTs)
title: Liposomal Irinotecan(Ⅱ), 5-FU/LV, and Cetuximab-β in First-Line Metastatic Colorectal Cancer

brief_summary:
Pregnancy is one of the most critical and unique events in a woman's life, resulting in changes in her appearance, social relationships, and family roles. During this period, certain physiological changes occur to support fetal growth, while psychological fluctuations that vary from the beginning to the end of pregnancy also occur. This process is particularly complicated in primigravida pregnant women due to a lack of knowledge, previous childbirth experience, and inaccurate and incomplete information received from others (1).

Tokophobia (from the Greek words "tokos," meaning birth, and "phobos," meaning fear) has been defined as "the fear and avoidance of childbirth despite desperately wanting a baby" (2,3). The fear of childbirth is a significant problem during pregnancy and after birth, and psychological and social factors are among the most influential factors. Tokophobia is a fear characterized by anxiety, often signaled by intense negative emotions and body expressions, and uncontrollable thoughts related to the cognitive aspect of anxiety (4). Tokophobia can be of two types: primary and secondary. A nulliparous woman's intense fear of childbirth can be classified as primary, while secondary tokophobia develops when a woman has a history of a previous traumatic obstetric event (2,5).

Bowby proposed that an innate psychobiological system (attachment behavior system) motivates the individual to seek closeness to supportive others (attachment figures) for protection and security in times of need (6). According to Ainsworth, people turn to attachment figures for two main reasons: a safe haven (i.e., the alleviation of distress and comfort) and a secure base from which to explore, learn, and grow (7). Attachment theory also identifies individual differences in attachment system functioning, often stemming from differences in experiences with attachment figures and the storage of these experiences in mental representations of self and others (8,9).

While social support is generalized to encompass individuals such as spouses, family, and friends, the support of the partner, who is the closest person to the pregnant woman, is among the most important social support systems for women. Spousal support is paramount in reducing fear of childbirth in pregnant women. Because fear of childbirth can lead to serious complications, spousal support plays a key role in a healthy pregnancy. Limited studies on the impact of spousal support on fear of childbirth during pregnancy have found that increased spousal support decreases fear of childbirth inversely proportional to increased spousal support (10,11). Studies have also shown that the relationship with spouses and social support have an impact on prenatal attachment (12,13).

The primary purpose of this study was to examine the impact of spousal support on tokophobia and attachment during pregnancy.
primary_outcomes: Wijma Delivery Expectancy/Experience Questionnaire Version A (W-DEQ-A) Score in Mothers
Prenatal Attachment Scale Score in Mothers
Fathers' Fear of Childbirth Scale Score
title: The Effect of Partner Support During Pregnancy on Tokophobia and Attachment
