brief_summary:
Stroke is a significant public health concern globally and a leading cause of long-term disability, affecting millions of people each year. According to the World Health Organization, approximately 15 million people worldwide suffer a stroke annually, resulting in about 5 million deaths and leaving another 5 million individuals with permanent disabilities. The prevalence of stroke is particularly alarming in Turkey. where recent studies estimate that over 150,000 strokes occur each year. This translates to a considerable burden on healthcare systems and highlights the urgent need for effective rehabilitation strategies to address the substantial number of individuals affected by stroke.

One of the most common impairments resulting from stroke is the loss of hand function, severely limiting a person's ability to therecovery of hand function is vital not only for restoring independence. As rehabilitation methods continue to evolve, innovative therapeutic approaches are being explored to optimize functional recovery in stroke patients.

Fine motor skills and hand function are critical components of rehabilitation for stroke patients, as they directly impact daily activities and overall independence. After a stroke, many patients experience impairments in motor control, which can lead to challenges in performing tasks requiring precision and dexterity, such as writing, grasping objects, or buttoning clothes. These impairments often result from damage to the brain areas responsible for motor coordination and sensation, particularly in the affected side of the body. Rehabilitation efforts focused on improving fine motor skills and hand function aim to enhance hand dexterity, increase grip strength, and restore the ability to perform functional tasks. Early and consistent therapy, including exercises that target fine motor movements, plays a vital role in promoting recovery and enhancing the patient's quality of life by fostering greater independence in both basic and complex activities.

Among these interventions, mirror therapy has garnered considerable attention for its potential to improve motor skills and functional outcomes. Mirror box therapy is a technique used to improve motor recovery in patients with upper/lower limb impairments, particularly in those with hemiplegia due to stroke or neurological conditions. Developed by Dr. Vilayanur S. Ramachandran, this method involves placing a mirror between the patient's limbs, allowing patients to observe the movement of their unaffected hand while simultaneously performing exercises . This visual feedback stimulates brain activity, aiding in neural recovery and enhancing functions like grip strength. This approach aims to create a visual illusion of movement in the affected limb, theraby stimulating neuroplasticity and promoting motor recovery.

Research has shown that mirror therapy can lead to significant improvements in hand function, coordination, and strength among stroke patients. It is a cost-effective, non-invasive technique that can easily be integrated into rehabilitation programs, making it accessible to a wide range of patients. Additionally, the psychological benefits associated with self-efficacy and motivation may further enhance the effectiveness of this therapeutic approach.

Therefore, This study aims to assess the effectiveness of mirror therapy in improving hand function among stroke patients, examining its impact on various functional outcomes and exploring the underlying mechanisms that contribute to recovery. By providing a comprehensive analysis of this innovative intervention. The uniqueness of this study lies in its focus on both grip strength and overall hand functionality, utilizing objective measures to assess the efficacy of mirror therapy in a population that often experiences significant motor deficits . By addressing these critical aspects of recovery, To improve quality of life for stroke survivors.

Hypothesis:

H₀: Mirror therapy has no significant additional effect on gross and fine motor skills, hand dexterity of the affected hand in patients with hemiplegia.

H₁: Mirror therapy has a significant additional effect on gross and fine motor skills, hand dexterity of the affected hand in patients with hemiplegia.
primary_outcomes: Box and Block Test
title: Efficacy of Mirror Therapy in Improving Hand Function and Fine Motor Skills in Hemiplegic Patients.

Congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (CNLDO) is a common condition in infants that may cause persistent tearing and mucopurulent discharge. Crigler massage is a conservative management technique performed by caregivers at home. Proper caregiver training and adherence to the recommended massage regimen may contribute to improved clinical outcomes.

This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a nurse-led step-by-step caregiver training program on Crigler massage adherence and clinical outcomes among infants with CNLDO.

Eligible caregiver-infant pairs will be randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group will receive a structured nurse-led training program involving theoretical instruction, practical demonstration, educational videos, an illustrated brochure, and follow-up reinforcement. The control group will receive standard care and routine instructions.

Caregivers' adherence will be assessed through massage frequency, number of strokes per session, and application of the recommended technique steps. Clinical outcomes will include resolution of CNLDO, epiphora, mucopurulent discharge, and the need for probing.

Participants will be followed for one month, and clinical outcomes will be evaluated by an ophthalmologist.

primary_outcomes: Overall Caregivers' Adherence to Crigler Massage (%)

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-controlled phase 3 study in participants with breast cancer. Participants scheduled to receive TC (docetaxel + cyclophosphamide) or TAC (docetaxel + doxorubicin + cyclophosphamide) chemotherapy will be randomized 1:1 (stratified by breast cancer stage \[early/advanced\] and chemotherapy regimen \[TC/TAC\]) to receive subcutaneous albipagrastim alfa 500 μg/kg at 24 hours (experimental group) or 48 hours (control group) after the end of chemotherapy administration in each 21-day chemotherapy cycle, for 4 cycles.

The main question it aims to answer is whether albipagrastim alfa administered 24 hours after chemotherapy is non-inferior to administration at 48 hours in preventing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, assessed by the duration of severe neutropenia (ANC \< 0.5 × 10\^9/L) in chemotherapy cycle 1.

Researchers will compare the two groups to see if 24-hour administration is as effective and safe as the approved 48-hour administration.

brief_summary:
Diaphragmatic hernias-whether congenital, traumatic, or iatrogenic-pose unique surgical challenges. While laparoscopic repair is standard, thoracoscopic (VATS) approaches offer superior visualization of the thoracic cavity and diaphragm. However, the optimal approach remains debated, particularly in complex or recurrent cases. Hybrid VATS-laparoscopy may offer enhanced visualization and safer reduction of herniated contents, but at the cost of increased invasiveness and operative time.

This study aims to evaluate whether VATS-only repair is a viable alternative to hybrid VATS-laparoscopy, focusing on perioperative outcomes and long-term recurrence.

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the effects of an 8-week stability-oriented proprioceptive exercise program (targeting the medial gastrocnemius), an 8-week reactive-oriented proprioceptive exercise program (targeting the lateral gastrocnemius), and a control condition on lower extremity muscle-tendon architecture, jumping performance, joint stability, dynamic balance, and proprioceptive perception in female volleyball players aged 16 to 20 years.

The study investigates whether stability-oriented and reactive-oriented proprioceptive training programs produce greater improvements in gastrocnemius muscle architecture, jumping performance, knee and ankle joint stability, dynamic balance, and joint position sense compared to a control group continuing routine volleyball training. Additionally, it evaluates the differential effects of the two exercise approaches on structural muscle adaptations and functional athletic performance parameters.

Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three groups: the Stability-Oriented Proprioceptive Exercise Group, the Reactive-Oriented Proprioceptive Exercise Group, or the Control Group. The two intervention groups will complete supervised 50-minute exercise sessions three times per week for 8 weeks in addition to their routine volleyball training, while the Control Group will continue only their routine volleyball training without additional proprioceptive exercises. Assessments will be performed at baseline (Week 0) and after the intervention (Week 8).
conditions: Lower Extremity Muscle Architecture and Jumping Performance
primary_outcomes: Change in Gastrocnemius Lateralis Muscle Thickness
Change in Gastrocnemius Lateralis Fascicle Length
title: Stability and Reactive Proprioceptive Training on Gastrocnemius Architecture and Jump Performance in Volleyball Players

brief_summary:
This project aims to study the treatments performed and long-term outcomes of the Myrhaug-Konjetzny treatment method (a combination of joint reconstruction and reconstruction of the articular disc in the temporomandibular joint) in patients with habitual dislocations of the temporomandibular joint.

The scientific questions were:

What treatment prognosis can be expected with the Myrhaug-Konjetzny method in patients with habitual temporomandibular joint (TMJ) dislocations? How have the participants experienced the long-term outcome? Is there any difference in the patient's experience depending on time from event (surgical treatment)? What is the frequency of additional surgical interventions in the TMJ among patients who have previously been treated with the Myrhaug-Konjetzny method for habitual TMJ dislocations? Are there any common factors in the patients' backgrounds that could be used in the future to identify suitable candidates for the treatment?
primary_outcomes: Number additional surgeries
title: TMJ Arthroplasty on Luxation

The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an online group singing intervention for older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is it feasible to deliver an online group singing intervention to older adults with MCI?
* Is the online group singing intervention acceptable and satisfactory to participants?

Researchers will compare online group singing with online music history education to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of the two programs and explore their effects on cognitive, emotional, and psychosocial outcomes.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to participate in either online group singing or online music history education.
* Attend regularly scheduled online group sessions.
* Complete questionnaires and assessments of cognitive function, emotional well-being, and psychosocial outcomes at designated study time points.

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate and compare the efficacy of Zinc supplementation and testosterone replacement therapy in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who have hypogonadism. Hypogonadism is a common hormonal complication in male patients with CKD and is characterized by reduced testosterone levels. It may contribute to fatigue, reduced sexual function, decreased muscle strength, and impaired quality of life. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to receive either zinc supplementation or testosterone replacement therapy according to the study protocol. The study will assess changes in serum testosterone levels and other predefined clinical parameters to compare the effectiveness of the two treatment approaches. The findings may help determine whether zinc supplementation could be a useful alternative to testosterone replacement therapy for managing hypogonadism in patients with CKD.

brief_summary:
Many university students experience poor sleep quality and frequently use smartphones shortly before going to sleep. This study aims to investigate whether replacing active smartphone use before bedtime with guided progressive muscle relaxation can improve sleep quality and related sleep behaviors.

A total of 152 university students aged 18-35 years with poor sleep quality and regular bedtime smartphone use will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Participants in the intervention group will perform a 27-minute audio-guided progressive muscle relaxation exercise five nights per week for four weeks. They will stop actively using their smartphones when starting the exercise and attempt to sleep without returning to active smartphone use afterward. Participants in the waitlist control group will continue their usual sleep and smartphone use habits.

Sleep quality, bedtime procrastination, pre-sleep arousal, and bedtime smartphone use will be assessed at baseline, after the four-week intervention, and at an additional four-week follow-up.

The study will examine whether this combined behavioral intervention improves sleep quality compared with usual habits and whether any observed changes persist after structured intervention support ends.
interventions: Progressive Muscle Relaxation and Bedtime Smartphone Use Reduction
primary_outcomes: Change in Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) Total Score From Baseline to Week 4

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to find out whether an artificial intelligence (AI) agent based on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves nurses' performance in managing postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). The participants are registered nurses working in the obstetric and gynecological ward, the obstetric emergency department and the critical care unit of Kafr Elsheikh General Hospital, Egypt.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Do nurses who use the RAG-based AI agent achieve higher performance scores in simulated PPH scenarios than nurses who use a printed guideline?
2. Do nurses who use the agent achieve higher PPH knowledge scores, complete more critical actions and perform them faster?

Researchers will compare the intervention group, which receives PPH education plus training on and four weeks of access to the AI agent, with the control group, which receives the same PPH education and a printed guideline booklet based on the World Health Organization (WHO) 2025 recommendations.

Participants will:

* Complete a PPH knowledge questionnaire and perform a video-recorded simulated PPH scenario at baseline, immediately after the training and after four weeks.
* Attend educational sessions on PPH (both groups) and training sessions on the AI agent (intervention group only).
* Use the AI agent in daily practice for four weeks (intervention group only) and rate its usability at the end of the study.
interventions: RAG-Based AI Agent for Postpartum Hemorrhage Management

Each visit includes resting baseline, viewing a virtual reality video, continued viewing during active or sham stimulation, and resting recovery. brief_summary: This clinical trial studies whether a group breathwork intervention works to improve chronic cancer-related pain (CCRP) in solid tumor cancer survivors. During the group breathwork intervention session in this trial, attendees are guided through breathwork in which they breathe in a continuous rhythm without pausing between inhale and exhale. brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the feasibility of a 12-week intensive group physiotherapy program for people with idiopathic Parkinson's disease. The program will be delivered in private physiotherapy practices and will consist of one 1-hour group session per week, with six participants per group.

People with Parkinson's disease commonly experience difficulties with walking, balance, posture, mobility, and other motor functions. Physiotherapy can help maintain or improve these abilities. However, in private practice, the usual format of individual physiotherapy sessions may limit the amount of intensive exercise that can be provided. This study will assess a group-based approach designed to provide prolonged and intensive motor training while adapting the exercises to each participant's abilities.

Each session will include nine 6-minute motor training stations performed with music. Participants will rotate between the different exercises under the supervision of physiotherapists. The program will consist of 12 weekly sessions over 12 weeks.

The main objective of the study is to assess whether this intensive group physiotherapy program is feasible in private physiotherapy practice. The primary outcome will be the proportion of participants completing at least 10 of the 12 sessions, a session being considered completed when the participant performs at least 7 of the 9 stations. The program will be considered feasible if at least 75% of participants meet this criterion. Attendance (proportion of participants attending at least 80% of the scheduled sessions) and the number of stations performed per session will also be reported.

The study will also explore changes in walking performance, functional abilities, balance, perception of Parkinson's disease severity, and quality of life between the beginning and the end of the program. Participants' satisfaction with the program will be assessed at the end of the study, and the physiotherapists delivering the intervention will also provide feedback on the program.

A total of 36 people with idiopathic Parkinson's disease, with a Hoehn and Yahr stage from 1 to 4, will participate in the study at two private physiotherapy practices. Participants will undergo assessments before and after the 12-week program.

The study is a prospective, two-center, open-label feasibility study.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility: proportion of participants completing at least 10 of the 12 sessions
title: Intensive Group Physiotherapy in People With Idiopathic Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary:
After surgery to repair the ligaments on the outer side of the ankle, patients are usually placed in a cast for two (or more) weeks and are not allowed to put weight on the foot. Some patients also have a damaged cartilage in the ankle joint. If so, this damage is usually treated in the same surgical intervention with microfracture. Recent studies suggest that moving the ankle and putting weight on it earlier may be safe, but no studies have included patients who have both types of injury.

This pilot study will test whether early movement and weight-bearing after surgery is feasible and safe. About 50 adults (aged 18-60) who are having arthroscopic ligament repair, with or without microfracture, will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will not have a cast. They will wear a supportive ankle brace and be allowed to put weight on the foot as pain allows from the first day after surgery. The other group will follow standard care at the hospital: a cast for two weeks without weight-bearing, followed by the same brace as the first group. From six weeks after surgery, both groups will follow the same rehabilitation.

We will measure how many eligible patients agree to take part, how well participants follow the program, how many drop out, and whether complications such as infection occur. We will also measure ankle function, pain, quality of life, range of motion, and return to work and sport, for up to 12 months after surgery. The results will help plan a larger study.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with postoperative complications
title: Early Weightbearing and Mobilization After Lateral Ankle Ligament Repair With or Without Microfracture of Talar Osteochondral Lesions: A Randomized Pilot Trial.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a 12-week Ayurvedic program can bring blood sugar back to the normal range in adults with prediabetes. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the Ayurvedic program help more people lower their HbA1c (a measure of average blood sugar over about three months) to below 5.7%, the normal range?
* Does the Ayurvedic program lower HbA1c, fasting blood sugar, weight, cholesterol, and blood pressure, and improve quality of life, more than a standard diabetes prevention program?

Researchers will compare the Ayurvedic program with a modified version of the National Diabetes Prevention Program (NDPP), a lifestyle education program, to see which works better.

Participants will:

* Take part in a 12-week program delivered online from home
* Attend weekly online group sessions and individual consultations
* In the Ayurvedic group: follow a personalized diet, take medicated ghee for five days, complete one day of supervised home-based therapeutic purgation (Virechana), and practice yoga
* In the NDPP group: attend weekly education sessions on healthy eating, physical activity, and stress management
* Have blood tests, weight, and blood pressure measured at the start and end of the program, and complete questionnaires about their health and well-being
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants Achieving HbA1c Below 5.7%
title: Ayurvedic Lifestyle Program Compared With a Diabetes Prevention Program for Adults With Prediabetes

brief_summary:
This study aims to understand outcomes and safety following injections used in everyday care for joint, tendon and other soft-tissue problems. Researchers will follow patients over two years to record changes in pain and movement, any complications, and whether further treatment is needed.

Approximately 500 adults aged 18 years or older will take part at participating MSK Doctors clinics in Grantham, Sleaford and London. Treatments include polyacrylamide hydrogel, hyaluronic acid, corticosteroid, platelet-rich plasma, platelet-rich fibrin and microfragmented adipose tissue injections.

Each patient and their clinician will decide on treatment before discussing participation in the research. This is an observational study: it records outcomes following the chosen treatment. Participants will not be randomly assigned to treatments, and the study will not change the injection or other care they receive.

Participants will complete a short pain score before their injection and approximately six weeks, three months, six months, 12 months and 24 months afterwards. Scores can be completed online, by telephone, by post or during a routine appointment.

Researchers will also collect relevant information from routine clinical records. This includes treatment details, complications, further treatment or surgery, and Motion Age results. Motion Age is a measure of movement and physical function produced by a camera-based assessment during normal clinical care.

Taking part adds research consent, pain scores and the use of relevant clinical information for research. It does not require additional injections, scans, tests or separate research appointments. Participation is voluntary, and deciding not to take part or withdrawing will not affect clinical care.

The findings will help patients and clinicians understand changes following musculoskeletal injection treatments and inform future care.
primary_outcomes: Change in Visual Analogue Scale Pain Score From Baseline to Six Months
title: Outcomes and Safety of MSK Injection Therapies in Routine Care

brief_summary:
Older adults who are malnourished or at risk of malnutrition may need help with eating after leaving hospital. Informal caregivers often provide this support, but may need practical nutrition advice.

This study evaluated whether nutrition education for caregivers could improve older adults' nutritional status over six months after hospital discharge.

This randomized study was conducted at the 251 Hellenic Air Force General Hospital in Athens, Greece. It included 240 patient-caregiver pairs. Patients were aged 65 years or older, lived in the community, and were malnourished or at risk of malnutrition according to the Mini Nutritional Assessment.

The pairs were randomly assigned to two equal groups. Both groups received usual hospital care, including discharge advice related to the patient's medical condition. In addition, caregivers in the intervention group received one individualized nutrition education session lasting approximately 25 minutes, delivered by a registered dietitian at discharge. They also received printed or electronic nutrition guidance, patient-specific recommendations, and weekly text-message reminders for six months.

The main outcome was patients' nutritional status, measured using the Mini Nutritional Assessment. Other outcomes were patients' quality of life, blood albumin and hemoglobin levels, and caregivers' quality of life. Assessments took place at baseline and six months.

brief_summary:
Primary spinal arachnoid webs and primary intradural arachnoid cysts are rare intradural pathologies that are increasingly recognized as distinct entities within the spectrum of spinal arachnopathies. Although uncommon, these lesions can have a substantial clinical impact because they may cause focal spinal cord compression and - through disturbance of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics - lead to progressive myelopathy, gait impairment, sensory and motor deficits, radicular pain, and, in advanced cases, sphincter dysfunction. In clinical practice, diagnostic delay and heterogeneity in symptom attribution are frequent challenges, partly because imaging findings may be subtle and because these pathologies are not consistently considered in the differential diagnosis of thoracic myelopathy.

Despite advances in imaging and increased awareness, there remains a paucity of high-quality prospective evidence guiding (i) treatment indications, (ii) expected clinical benefit versus risks of surgery, and (iii) the natural history under conservative management.

The purpose of the WEBCAST trial is to prospectively evaluate the clinical course, radiological evolution, and safety outcomes of primary spinal arachnoid webs and primary intradural arachnoid cysts under real-world conditions within a German-speaking multicenter network. Specifically, the trial aims to determine whether surgical management (e.g., microsurgical web release/resection or cyst fenestration/partial resection) is associated with superior functional and patient-reported outcomes compared with conservative management, while systematically capturing complications and radiological trajectories.

All patients presenting to a participating site with clinical and imaging findings consistent with a primary arachnoid web or primary intradural arachnoid cyst will be screened consecutively. Patients who signed the Informed Consent will complete questionnaires (Modified McCormick scale, QoL: EQ-5D-5L, Patient-reported symptoms: structured symptom inventory + NRS pain and NPS) at baseline, 3 months and 12 months by the treating physician using standardized definitions. If available, gait aids and work status/function will be documented as supportive descriptors. An MRI of the spine will be performed at baseline, 3 months and 12 months. Treatment of webs is according to standard care of the participating site.
lead_sponsor: Insel Gruppe AG, University Hospital Bern
primary_outcomes: Modified McCormick Scale
title: WEBCAST: Webs and Cysts - Arachnopathy Study A Prospective Multicenter Observational Registry Study

mPET imaging is a type of PET scan that can obtain imaging of 2-4 radiotracers at the same time. Standard PET scans can only obtain imaging of 1 radiotracer at a time (such as an 18F-FDG scan or an 124I scan). The researchers think that mPET may be a better way to image cancer because it will allow researchers to see multiple radiotracers on the same images and will reduce the number of scans needed to obtain the images.

brief_summary:
Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is an important technique for treating severe coronary artery disease, often serving as the final option to improve quality of life and extend survival for patients. Among patients undergoing CABG, the 10-year patency rate for internal mammary artery (IMA) grafts can reach 90%, compared to 40%-50% for venous grafts. Currently, the utilization rate of IMA grafts in isolated CABG patients in China lags significantly behind international region. Furthermore, substantial variations exist across hospitals, representing a critical quality issue in cardiac surgical care.

This study aims to develop a comprehensive intervention package to improve the utilization of IMA grafts in CABG patients. Targeting hospitals performing CABG as the intervention units, with CABG patients as the beneficiaries, the study will evaluate the effectiveness of this intervention in increasing IMA grafts use in China. The primary outcome measure is the proportion of patients receiving at least one IMA grafts. Secondary outcome measures include perioperative patient outcomes. A stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial design will be employed to implement the intervention. Participating hospitals will be randomly assigned to cross from the control to the intervention phase. Timely feedback of usage rate of IMA grafts will be used to support cause analysis, refine management, and ultimately enhance the quality of care for CABG patients.

primary_outcomes: Rate of internal mammary artery graft utilization among patients undergoing isolated CABG during hospitalization
title: Increasing the Use of Internal Mammary Artery Grafting

brief_summary:
Mal de débarquement syndrome (MdDS) is a balance disorder that can make people feel as if they are rocking, swaying, or bobbing even when they are still. For some people, symptoms begin after travel or other exposure to motion. For others, symptoms begin without a clear motion trigger. This study included adults with both forms of persistent MdDS whose symptoms had not improved enough after a previous treatment that used moving visual patterns and head movements.

The study compared two forms of galvanic vestibular stimulation (GVS). GVS uses a weak electrical current delivered through pads placed on the skin behind the ears. The current changes signals from the balance system. One group received a steady current, called direct-current GVS. The other group received a current that varied randomly, called noisy GVS. The term "noisy" describes how the current varied. Participants were assigned by chance to one of the two groups and were not told which type they received. Both groups received active stimulation.

The researchers first measured the current level at which each participant began to feel a movement sensation. They then tested several current levels in short sessions and measured symptoms and standing balance before and after each test. They used those measurements to choose a current level for each participant. Participants then attended one 20-minute session per day for five consecutive days.

The main symptom of interest was how strongly participants felt they were moving. Participants rated this sensation immediately before and after each daily session. The researchers examined how many participants rated the sensation at least half as severe at the end of the treatment week as they did before the first session. They also measured how much participants swayed while standing on a balance platform with their eyes closed.

Participants answered brief questions on their phones during the week before treatment, during the five treatment days, and for one month afterward. These questions covered perceived movement, nausea, sensitivity to visual stimuli, difficulty thinking clearly, mood, stress, anxiety, and energy. Longer questionnaires asked about how dizziness affected daily activities, general health, and emotional well-being. The researchers also recorded side effects and asked participants about physical and emotional discomfort during treatment.

The researchers expected the five-day schedule to be practical and tolerable and expected that at least some participants would report less perceived movement. The study was designed to compare the two personalized approaches and describe symptom changes during treatment and follow-up. Because everyone received active stimulation, the study could not determine how much of any change was due to stimulation itself.

Change From Baseline in Standing Sway Confidence Ellipse Area
title: Comparing Two Types of Galvanic Vestibular Stimulation in Mal de Débarquement Syndrome

All patients in the study will have blood collected during surgery to measure baseline metal ion levels. Patients will also have standardized follow-up visits. This information will help answer specific U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) questions about metal exposure in the body and additional surgeries after VerteGlide treatment.

Patients will be placed into one of two groups:

Asymptomatic Post-Operative Cohort: Patients who do not have symptoms that require another surgery.

Subsequent Surgical Intervention (SSI) Cohort: Patients who have a planned or unplanned additional surgery.

During the study, some patients may move from the Asymptomatic Post-Operative Cohort to the SSI Cohort if they need another surgery.

Before any study-specific procedures are performed, informed consent will be obtained from the patient's parent or legal guardian. The patient will also provide assent when appropriate.

The study is designed to follow the usual care for children with EOS as much as possible. This will reduce extra visits and procedures for patients and their families and may help patients remain in the study.

brief_summary: Medial meniscus posterior root tears cause loss of hoop tension, meniscal extrusion and rapid progression of knee osteoarthritis. Transtibial pullout repair is the most commonly used treatment, but there is no consensus on whether the tibial tunnel should be drilled from the anteromedial or the anterolateral tibial cortex. The anterolateral (lateral) tunnel may better follow the natural pull direction of the root and reduce the acute suture angle at the tunnel aperture. The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to compare medial and lateral tibial tunnels in terms of change in medial meniscal extrusion on MRI 12 months after surgery, as well as tunnel position, root healing and functional outcomes.

brief_summary:
Dietary oils differ in their fatty acid composition, and their effects on the gut microbiota remain unclear. Early findings suggest that different oils may alter the abundance of certain bacterial groups. However, little is known about palm mid fraction (PMF) and palm kernel oil (PKO), or how their effects compare with commercially available vegetable oils and fats.

In this proof-of-concept study, healthy volunteers will consume a meal prepared with palm olein and provide faecal samples. The samples will be used as inoculum to establish an in vitro digestion and fermentation system. This system will then compare palm olein, PMF and PKO with selected commercially available oils and fats under the same laboratory conditions.

The study will assess changes in gut microbiota composition and short-chain fatty acid production. It aims to determine whether palm-derived oils show comparable or greater effects than the other oils tested, and whether the system is suitable for screening a wider range of dietary fats. The findings will help identify which oils warrant further study in humans.
primary_outcomes: Gut microbiota composition
title: Exploring the Potential Prebiotic Properties of Palm Oil Fractions, Palm Kernel Oil (PKO) and Commercially Available Vegetable Oils and Fats

brief_summary: Ulcerative colitis (UC) results from a dynamic imbalance between the intestinal microbiota, the epithelial barrier and the immune system. In a pediatric UC cohort, the team identified alternative stable states (ASS) of the intestinal ecosystem: favourable, diverse states associated with remission, and depleted and dysbiotic states associated with active disease and a higher risk of treatment failure or relapse. CHARTS is a prospective, multicentric cohort that aims to translate and validate the concept of alternative holobiont states in adult UC patients who are naive to biotherapy and for whom a biotherapy is indicated as standard of care. One hundred patients will be followed for one year (visits at W0, W14, W30, W52) with longitudinal clinical data, blood and fecal samples and 2-3 standard-of-care endoscopies. Fecal microbiota will be characterized by sequencing and intestinal inflammation by fecal calprotectin. The project will build an integrative reference framework of intestinal ecosystem states and an algorithm to attribute a microbiota state from a single fecal sample, in order to identify patients likely to benefit from future microbiota-targeting (symbio-) therapy. No symbiotherapy will be initiated or proposed during the study.
primary_outcomes: Microbiota state attribution from fecal taxonomic composition (16S DNA sequencing).

brief_summary:
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, caused by various metabolic factors. \[1,2\]MASLD can progress to liver fibrosis, and even liver cancer or liver failure, through metabolic-associated fatty liver hepatitis (MASH). \[3,4\]Therefore, timely and accurate diagnosis of MAFLD and MASH is crucial.

Liver biopsy (LB) is the gold standard for diagnosing hepatic steatosis and MASH in MASLD.\[5\] However, as an invasive procedure, it has limitations such as the risk of bleeding, sampling errors, and the inability to repeat the examination in the short term. \[6\]Imaging techniques are commonly used non-invasive methods for assessing hepatic steatosis. The application of quantitative CT makes it easier to detect hepatic steatosis\[7\], but it involves radiation exposure during the examination. Studies have shown\[8-10\] that proton density fat fraction (PDFF) is an alternative method to LB for accurately quantifying hepatic steatosis, but it is costly and time-consuming. Therefore, it is necessary to find a non-invasive, accurate, and cost-effective method for evaluating MASLD and MASH.

title: UGAP Diagnosis of Hepatic Steatosis in MASLD

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to compare two ultrasound methods for identifying nerves in the armpit. Researchers will examine whether following a nerve along the arm makes it easier to identify in the armpit. The study will include 80 healthy volunteers aged 18-65 who work at Hacettepe University Faculty of Medicine.

Ultrasound uses sound waves to create images of structures inside the body. It does not use radiation. Identifying nerves in the armpit helps doctors plan nerve blocks. These are injections near nerves to numb the arm for surgery or pain relief. This study involves ultrasound scans only; participants will not receive nerve blocks.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does nerve tracking allow researchers to identify the nerves more often than cross-sectional scanning?
* Which method provides clearer images of the nerves?
* How long does each method take to identify the nerves?
* How closely do two researchers agree on nerve visibility and location using each method?

Researchers will compare two methods in each participant:

* Cross-sectional scanning: The researcher places the ultrasound probe in the armpit to identify the nerves directly.
* Nerve tracking: The researcher first identifies each nerve near the elbow or along the upper arm. They then follow the nerve with the ultrasound probe toward the armpit.

Both methods will examine the same three nerves: the median, ulnar, and radial nerves. These nerves help control movement and sensation in the arm and hand. Researchers will record whether they can see each nerve and rate its image clarity. They will also record each nerve's location relative to the main artery in the armpit. Other measurements include the time needed to identify the nerves and their depth beneath the skin.

Participants will:

* Attend two visits at least 21 days apart. The second visit is planned to take place within 60 days of the first.
* Have both ultrasound scans at each visit, with a rest of at least 15 minutes between scans.
* Have the scans performed on their dominant arm, usually the arm they use for writing.
* Lie on their back and position their arm as directed. The researcher will apply ultrasound gel and move the probe over the skin.
* Provide basic health and demographic information, such as age and medical history.
* Have their height, weight, and upper arm circumference measured. Two experienced researchers will perform the scans independently. Each researcher will use one method at the first visit and the other method at the second. This means both researchers will use both methods on each participant during the study. The initial researcher-method pairing and the scan order at each visit will be chosen by chance. Researchers will not see each other's findings or their own previous measurements when performing the scans.

People with previous arm trauma, surgery, or peripheral nerve injury will not be eligible. Other exclusions include nerve disorders and conditions that prevent the required arm positioning. People with a mass, deformity, active infection, or skin lesion in the armpit will also be excluded.

Participants will not receive injections or medicines. No blood, tissue, or other biological samples will be collected. Probe pressure or holding the arm in position may cause temporary discomfort or tiredness. Scans will take place in a private room, with only the necessary area exposed.

Participation is voluntary, and participants may leave the study at any time. Taking part is not expected to provide a direct health benefit. The findings may help doctors choose methods for identifying and locating nerves before future nerve block procedures.
conditions: Ultrasound Identification of Peripheral Nerves at the Axillary Level
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Nerves Successfully Visualized at the Axillary Level
title: Comparison of Cross-Sectional Scanning and Nerve Tracking Techniques for Ultrasonographic Identification of the Terminal Branches of the Brachial Plexus at the Axillary Level: A Prospective Observational Study

brief_summary: The ADAPTO study is a pilot trial where 6 participants receiving liver SABR treatment will be recruited. Participants will have MRI scans before treatment, then 1 week, 1 month, 3 months and 6 months after treatment, focusing partiuclarly on diffusion imaging (which creates a map of water movement over the imaging region). Since tumours are structured differently from healthy tissue, they look different on diffusion maps. Previous studies show that changes to the tumour caused by treatment should be visible on diffusion maps earlier after treatment than using the methods used at the moment to watch tumour response to treatment. This study will analyse the diffusion maps (both qualitatively and quantitatively) before and after treatment to investigate when tumour response can be detected and assessed using this imaging method compared with the standard follow up processes in use clinically. If tumour response can be accurately assessed at an earlier point than standard follow up processes when using diffusion imaging, this opens up possibilities to use this technique to reduce the time patients wait to know if their treatment has been effective and make clinical decision making possible at an earlier stage.

title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient as A Predictor of Liver SABR Treatment Outcome

The study will enroll competitively up to 56 patients with RAI-refractory DTCs after progression to standard therapies, at least one or two prior treatment lines with multikinase inhibitors (MKIs) including sorafenib, lenvatinib and/or cabozantinib. A previous study involving patients who had undergone abdominal surgery demonstrated an immediate improvement in ventilation and oxygen saturation following an ABDOWN session. Further research is now required to continue evaluating this method.

The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effects of various mobilization positions, including ABDOWN, on lung volume, blood gases, and the distribution of ventilation in patients who have undergone cardiac surgery and are at high risk for pulmonary complications, as well as in a group of matched controls.

Undergo laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy under general anesthesia.

Be randomly assigned to one of two ventilation strategies after induction:

Have arterial blood gases and respiratory mechanics parameters measured preoperatively, intraoperatively (every 10 minutes), and postoperatively.

The goal of this mechanistic clinical trial is to define nitric oxide-dependent mechanisms for sex-specific autonomic dysregulation in older adults with hypertension. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Whether nitric oxide bioavailability modulates peripheral sympathetic adrenergic control during orthostatic stress? What is the role of nitric oxide bioavailability in reflex blood pressure buffering?

Older men and women with hypertension will be randomly assigned to receive either dietary nitrate supplementation (beetroot juice) or placebo for 8 weeks. Before surgery, participants will have fasting blood tests to measure serum uric acid and undergo shoulder MRI to assess tendon tear size, retraction, and fatty infiltration. brief_summary:
REMEND-CO is a prospective, single-center, single-arm, open-label pilot feasibility study designed to assess the implementation of a structured psychocorporal relaxation program in older adults with Alzheimer's disease or related neurodegenerative disorders and clinically observed agitation, hospitalized in a Cognitive Behavioral Unit.

The study aims to enroll 30 participants aged 65 years or older. In addition to usual care, participants will be offered eight individual relaxation sessions, delivered approximately once weekly over eight weeks by a trained psychomotor therapist.

The primary objective is to assess the feasibility of implementing the program in routine clinical practice. Feasibility will be evaluated through recruitment, session attendance and completion, treatment discontinuations, tolerability, adverse events, and adaptations required during implementation.

Secondary objectives include describing organizational constraints and exploring changes in agitation, neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disturbances, and psychotropic medication prescriptions. Clinical assessments will include the Cohen-Mansfield Agitation Inventory (CMAI), Neuropsychiatric Inventory-Nursing Home Version (NPI-ES), and Sleep Disorders Scale for Dementia (SDSD).

A qualitative component involving semi-structured interviews with participants and, where appropriate, their relatives will explore the experience and acceptability of the program.

All analyses will be primarily descriptive and exploratory. As this study has no control group, it is not designed to establish clinical efficacy or a causal effect of the intervention.

brief_summary:
Complex post-traumatic stress disorder (cPTSD) is a severe and often persistent mental disorder associated with substantial functional impairment following prolonged or repeated traumatic experiences, particularly interpersonal childhood trauma. Trauma-focused cognitive behavioural interventions, including Imagery Rescripting (ImR), are recommended first-line treatments for trauma-related symptoms. ImR is an established imagination-based intervention that typically comprises several phases, including (1) reactivating the traumatic memory, (2) observing the situation from the perspective of the current adult self, (3) intervening to protect and support the younger self, (4) providing comfort and compassion to the younger self, and (5) creating a meaningful positive closing image. Although the mechanisms underlying ImR are not yet fully understood, several process-related factors have been proposed as mechanisms of change, including reductions in shame, guilt, maladaptive self-referential cognitions, and experiential avoidance, as well as increases in self-compassion. The self-comforting phase 4 is considered particularly relevant to these processes, as it directly targets compassionate engagement with one's younger self. However, this phase relies heavily on the ability to generate vivid mental imagery, which can be challenging for some individuals.

Virtual reality (VR) may facilitate these therapeutic processes by providing immersive, embodied, and highly self-relevant experiences. In the present study, participants interact with an individualized AI-generated 360° representation of their younger self created from a childhood photograph.

The present study aims to investigate and compare participants' responses to conventional imagery-based and VR-supported delivery of the self-comforting phase 4 of ImR in adults with cPTSD. In one condition, this phase is conducted entirely in imagination, as in standard ImR. In the other condition, patients use a virtual reality (VR) headset to interact with a personalized 360-degree representation of their younger self, generated from a childhood photograph. They subsequently switch perspectives to experience their adult self providing comfort and compassion to their younger self. All other phases of ImR are conducted identically in imagination in both conditions.

Ten adults with cPTSD who are already receiving outpatient trauma-focused treatment will each participate in four ImR sessions over two weeks: two sessions using conventional imagery-based ImR and two sessions using VR-supported ImR, with the order of conditions randomized. Participants complete weekly online questionnaires for several weeks before and after the sessions.

During the two-week intervention period, participants complete brief smartphone-based questionnaires five times daily to assess their symptoms, emotions, and self-related thoughts in everyday life (ecological momentary assessment, EMA). Before and after each session, participants briefly recall the targeted memory while their emotional responses and physiological signals (heart rate and skin conductance) are recorded. At the end of the study, participants take part in an interview to share their experiences.

The study primarily examines whether self-compassion, shame, guilt, negative self-related thoughts, and avoidance change over the course of the study, as assessed through questionnaires and daily-life assessments (EMA). It also investigates whether these changes differ between the imagery-based and VR-supported conditions and evaluates the feasibility and tolerability of the VR-supported approach.

German State Self-Compassion Scale - Short Form (SSCS-S) subscale and composite scores (Ecological Momentary Assessment, EMA)

brief_summary:
Children are exposed to various painful procedures. The most feared of these procedures is suturing because of the fear and pain experienced and the long intervention time. Although there are various studies in the literature on the efficacy of distraction in children, there are a limited number of studies evaluating the effectiveness of the methods applied during suturing. Therefore, the aim of this study was to investigate the effect of blowing a wind vane or cognitive-behavioral combined programs with interactive robots on the fear and pain that children aged 4-12 years who applied to the pediatric emergency department for incision suturing.

As a result of this study, the most useful distraction method for the 4-12 age group will be decided by paying attention to cost-effectiveness ratios in painful procedures that may be traumatic in children such as suture procedures. It is known that the earlier the traumas experienced by children, the deeper they become. Thanks to this research, the way to alleviate the traumas experienced will be sought and the formation of permanent scars will be prevented.
primary_outcomes: Fear average score
Pain average score
title: Wind Rose and Interactive Robots

brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to evaluate whether a structured, family-based Mediterranean-style dietary intervention can improve household dietary patterns among first-degree relatives (parents and siblings) of children newly diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the intervention improve adherence to a Mediterranean-style dietary pattern, as measured by the Mediterranean Diet Adherence Score (MEDAS), from baseline to 6 months?
* Does the intervention reduce the consumption of ultra-processed foods, as assessed using the NOVA classification?
* Are dietary changes associated with changes in fecal calprotectin levels and gut microbiome composition and diversity?

Participants will:

* Attend an initial in-person consultation with a clinical dietitian.
* Complete an online food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) and a general lifestyle questionnaire.
* Receive standardized dietary education based on Mediterranean-style dietary principles.
* Participate in dietitian-led follow-up sessions via telemedicine every 2 months for at least 6 months.
* Complete dietary assessments at baseline and at 2, 4, and 6 months.
* Provide stool samples at baseline, 2 months, and 6 months for fecal calprotectin measurement and gut microbiome and metabolomics characterization.
conditions: First-degree Relatives (Parents and Siblings) of Children Newly Diagnosed With Inflammatory Bowel Disease
primary_outcomes: Change in Mediterranean Diet Adherence Score (MEDAS)
Change in Ultra-Processed Food Consumption (NOVA Group 4)
title: Family-Based Mediterranean Diet Intervention in First-Degree Relatives of Children With IBD

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to examine the effects of a psychoeducation program designed by the researcher to regulate social rhythms on biological rhythms and functioning in individuals diagnosed with bipolar disorder.

Do participants who take part in the psychoeducation program aimed at regulating social rhythms have higher scores on the Bipolar Disorder Functioning Scale? Do participants who take part in the psychoeducation program aimed at regulating social rhythms have lower scores on the Biological Rhythm Interview of Assessment? In order to evaluate the effects of the psychoeducation program consisting of nine sessions aimed at regulating social rhythms, the intervention group was compared with a control group that received a single-session experience-sharing intervention.
interventions: Psychoeducation Program for Social Rhythm Regulation
primary_outcomes: Bipolar disorders functioning scale
Biological Rhythms Interview of Assessment in Neuropsychiatry (BRIAN)
title: Impact of Social Rhythm Psychoeducation on Biological Rhythm and Functioning in Bipolar Disorder

The program is intended to offer pre-approval access to sonesitatug vedotin for patients who have received at least one prior line of therapy.
title: An Early Access Program of Sonesitatug Vedotin as Second-Line or Later Treatment for Patients With CLDN18.2-Expressing Advanced or Metastatic Gastric, Gastroesophageal Junction, or Oesophageal Adenocarcinoma

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study is to investigate how the injection technique influences the distribution of an injected substance within a lymph node in healthy volunteers. The study aims to improve the understanding of intralymphatic injections, which are used in intralymphatic immunotherapy (ILIT), an approach employed for the treatment of allergies and in cancer vaccine research.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How do different injection volumes, needle designs and injection sites affect the distribution of the injected substance within the lymph node?
* Does any of the injected substance flow back out of the lymph node or into the surrounding tissue?
* How much of the substance is taken up by the lymph node, and does it migrate to other lymph nodes?
* How feasible and reproducible is the ultrasound-guided injection procedure?

Participants will:

* Receive a small injection of an already approved, weakly radioactive-labeled protein (99mTc-HSA) into a lymph node in the groin under ultrasound guidance.
* Undergo imaging examinations (scintigraphy and SPECT/CT) to assess the distribution and migration of the injected substance.
* Remain under medical supervision during and after the procedure to monitor for possible adverse reactions.
conditions: Assessment of the Dispersion Pattern of a Radiolabelled Protein in Human Inguinal Lymph Nodes
interventions: Ultrasound-Guided Intralymphatic Injection of Radiolabelled Protein

Intranodal Distribution Pattern of Radiolabelled Protein - Localisation
Internodal Migration of Radiolabelled Protein
title: Biodistribution of Compounds After Intralymphatic Injection

brief_summary:
Hysterectomy may have psychological implications for women, including changes in body image, reproductive identity, and perceptions of meaning in life. This randomized, two-group, parallel-group trial aimed to evaluate the effects of a logotherapy-based nursing intervention on meaning in life and body image among women following hysterectomy.

A total of 140 women who underwent hysterectomy at Menoufia University Hospital and Al-Qasr Teaching Hospital in Shebin El-Kom, Menoufia Governorate, Egypt, were randomly allocated to an intervention group (n = 70) or a control group receiving routine postoperative care (n = 70). The intervention consisted of eight logotherapy-based nursing sessions delivered twice weekly over four weeks, with each session lasting approximately 60 minutes. The sessions addressed personal meaning, sources of meaning, coping with loss, and future goal setting.

Participants completed baseline and post-intervention assessments. Meaning in life was assessed using the Meaning in Life Questionnaire, including the Presence of Meaning and Search for Meaning subscales. Body image was assessed using the Body Self-Image Questionnaire-Short Form. The study compared post-intervention outcomes between the two groups, adjusting for baseline scores, to evaluate the effects of the nursing intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Meaning in Life Scores from Baseline to Immediately Post-Intervention
title: Effect of Logotherapy-Based Nursing on Meaning in Life and Body Image After Hysterectomy

brief_summary: This study will compare two inflation durations of a perfusion drug-coated balloon in people with previously untreated coronary artery lesions. The balloon is designed to allow some blood flow during inflation. The study will assess whether keeping the balloon inflated for at least 90 seconds, compared with 30 to 60 seconds, reduces narrowing of the treated artery at 12 months. A total of 360 participants will be randomly assigned to the two groups after successful lesion preparation. The main assessment will use quantitative coronary angiography performed by assessors who do not know the treatment assignment. Procedural outcomes, clinical events, bleeding, and selected intravascular imaging findings will also be evaluated.

primary_outcomes: In-segment late lumen loss at 12 months

brief_summary: This study is an experimental, prospective, two-arm randomized study. The objective of this case study is to develop a Value-Based Healthcare framework for people with multiple sclerosis (MS), specifically targeting young patients (≤40 years old) with a relapsing-remitting disease course. Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) will be collected through national MS Care Unit(s) focused on neurorehabilitation treatments and used together with Patient Reported Experience Measures (PREMs) and Patient Preference Information (PPI) to determine whether a high-performing national MS Care Unit in terms of PROMs and/or PREMS and/or PPI generates an impact on direct or indirect healthcare cost. The investigators aim to collect information about the use of the selected outcomes across MS Care Unit rehabilitation facilities at the national level via a tailored web-survey that can be implemented as a service to maximise access to and increase effectiveness of multidisciplinary rehabilitation in young people with MS. This service allows the seamless accumulation of global data, in a digitized format which can be used as input for digital and statistical analyses. The investigators will engage different stakeholders (healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, industry and academics) to adopt a framework for meaningful patient and public involvement in improving access to neurorehabilitation treatments and informing service design.
interventions: "Enhanced support" intervention in parallel with multidisciplinary rehabilitation

World Health Organisation Quality of Life Measure (WHOQOL-100)

brief_summary:
Title: The Effect of Reiki Application on Caregiving Outcomes and Coping with Stress in Caregivers of Palliative Care Patients: A Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial

This study was conducted as a single-blind, parallel-arm, randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effect of distant Reiki application on caregiving outcomes and coping with stress among informal caregivers of palliative care patients.

The trial has been completed with a total of 44 caregivers who were randomly assigned to either the Reiki intervention group (n=23) or the control group (n=21). In addition to routine care, participants in the intervention group received distant Reiki administered by certified researchers under the supervision of a Reiki Master Teacher over a 3-week period. The control group received routine care without any complementary intervention.

Data were collected at baseline (pre-intervention) and at the end of the 3rd week (immediately post-intervention) using the Bakas Caregiving Outcomes Scale (BCOS) and the Stress Coping Methods Scale (SCMS). The study aimed to examine the potential supportive role of Reiki in improving caregiving outcomes and stress coping mechanisms within a controlled research design.
primary_outcomes: Stress Coping Strategies and Level
title: The Effect of Reiki on Caregivers

brief_summary:
After giving birth, a woman is more likely than usual to develop a blood clot in a vein, especially in the first few weeks. Blood clots like this are uncommon, but they can be serious. Nexplanon is a small contraceptive implant placed under the skin of the arm. It releases a hormone called etonogestrel and does not contain estrogen. Its product label suggests waiting 3 to 4 weeks after delivery before getting the implant. However, several health organizations say that hormone-only birth control can be used right after delivery, before leaving the hospital.

This study looks at whether getting Nexplanon right after delivery changes the chance of a blood clot in the first 28 days after leaving the hospital. Researchers will compare two groups of women who gave birth in a US hospital. One group received Nexplanon before going home. The other group received no prescribed birth control before going home. The goal is to find out whether the implant leads to a meaningfully higher chance of blood clots than no birth control.

This study does not enroll anyone or give any treatment. It uses existing health records and insurance claims from women who gave birth during the defined period. Their personal identities are removed from the data.
primary_outcomes: Acute venous thromboembolism
title: Immediate Postpartum Nexplanon Placement and Risk of Venous Thromboembolism

Participants will undergo four weeks of individualized visual rehabilitation delivered three times per week in addition to usual multidisciplinary rehabilitation care. Outcomes will be assessed before and after the intervention. The study uses an exploratory multiple-case design, and results will primarily be interpreted at the individual participant level.
primary_outcomes: Change in Head Lateral Flexion
Change in Shoulder Inclination
Change in Trunk Lateral Inclination
title: Postural Changes After Stroke in Patients With Visual Disorders

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial evaluates whether a perioperative tailored exercise program prevents or reduces bowel dysfunction, including low anterior resection syndrome (LARS), in patients with stage I-III rectal cancer undergoing low anterior resection (LAR) with primary anastomosis and without a stoma.

A total of 92 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to an exercise group or a control group. The exercise group receives standard postoperative care plus a phase-specific exercise program: a preoperative orientation, supervised in-hospital sessions from postoperative day 1 until discharge, home-based exercise 5 times per week with online coaching twice a week until 3 months after surgery, and self-directed home-based exercise monitored through a mobile application until 12 months after surgery. The control group receives standard postoperative care only.

The primary outcome is the change in LARS score from baseline (before surgery) to 6 months after surgery. Secondary outcomes include anorectal manometry, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-CR29), physical activity (GPAQ), physical function, body composition, and LARS score and quality of life at 12 months after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in LARS score at 6 months after surgery
title: Perioperative Tailored Exercise for Bowel Function After Low Anterior Resection in Rectal Cancer

brief_summary:
Hashimoto's thyroiditis is an autoimmune disease affecting the thyroid gland. Changes in the gut microbiota may be associated with autoimmune thyroid disorders. However, it remains unclear whether supplementation with specific beneficial bacterial strains can improve health-related outcomes in women with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.

The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of six weeks of psychobiotic supplementation on quality of life, self-reported symptoms, thyroid function, oxidative stress markers, body composition, blood pressure, and dietary habits.

A total of 78 adult women reporting a previous diagnosis of Hashimoto's thyroiditis were randomly assigned to receive either a psychobiotic supplement containing Lactobacillus helveticus R0052 and Bifidobacterium longum R0175 (3 billion colony-forming units (3 x 10\*9 CFU) per day) or a placebo.

The study was double-blind, meaning that neither the participants nor the researchers conducting the assessments knew which supplement each participant received. Measurements were performed before and after the six-week intervention.

Self-reported symptoms included sleepiness, constipation, bloating and gas, cold intolerance, and concentration difficulties. Seventy-one participants completed the follow-up assessment.
interventions: Placebo Capsule(s) Once a Day by Mouth
primary_outcomes: Change in WHOQOL-BREF Physical Health Domain Score
Change in WHOQOL-BREF Psychological Health Domain Score
Change in WHOQOL-BREF Social Relationships Domain Score
Change in WHOQOL-BREF Environment Domain Score

brief_summary: Autoimmune diseases and autoimmune cytopenias are rare conditions. However, patients with these conditions represent a significant portion of our department's active patient population as part of the work carried out by our constituent rare disease reference centers. While our understanding of the pathophysiology of these diseases is growing year by year, many questions remain unanswered, such as predicting whether a condition will become chronic, the occurrence of long-term complications, the risk of relapse, and, above all, the response to treatment. With the goal of personalized medicine aimed at improving overall patient care, the identification of predictive biomarkers is a major objective, recognized by the entire medical and scientific community, and currently represents an unmet medical need. With this in mind, the establishment of biobanks linked to precise phenotypic data is essential to enable the rapid conduct of translational studies in light of evolving scientific knowledge.
primary_outcomes: Comparison of patients' biological samples collected before and after the start of treatment, based on their clinical course (remission, relapse, chronicity).
title: Cohort Study of Patients With Autoimmune Diseases: A Longitudinal Study to Identify Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Theranostic Markers

title: Association Between Alzheimer Biomarker (Amyloid Beta-42) And Periodontitis in Geriatric Patients

brief_summary:
This study aims to determine whether melatonin can reduce the occurrence of seizures in term newborn babies with moderate hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), a condition in which the brain is affected due to reduced oxygen and blood supply around the time of birth.

A total of 98 eligible newborns will be enrolled in this randomized controlled trial at the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), Department of Pediatrics, King Edward Medical University / Mayo Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Newborns in the intervention group will receive a single dose of 10 mg melatonin, given through a nasogastric tube within the first six hours after birth, in addition to routine medical care. Newborns in the control group will receive routine medical care alone.

Parents or guardians will be unaware of the treatment group assigned to their baby. All newborns will be monitored for the first 72 hours of life to assess whether seizures occur. The study will also evaluate the time of the first seizure, number and duration of seizure episodes, and the need for anti-seizure medications.

The main hypothesis is that melatonin, when given in addition to routine medical care, will reduce the occurrence of seizures during the first 72 hours of life in term newborns with moderate HIE compared with routine medical care alone.
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of clinically observed seizures (Yes/No)
title: Melatonin for Reducing Seizures in Term Neonates With Moderate Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy

brief_summary: The aim of this analysis was to pool individual participant-level baseline data from seven independent studies conducted in Brazil to characterize the biophysical properties of facial skin in Brazilian women using instrumental measurements and investigate their associations with Fitzpatrick skin phototype, age group, and geographic location. This characterization aims to improve understanding of skin diversity in Brazil and support the development of more inclusive, effective cosmetic products tailored to the needs of the Brazilian population. This secondary pooled analysis was planned and conducted after the completion of all seven independent studies.
primary_outcomes: Mean facial skin hydration measured by corneometry according to skin phototype, age group, and geographic location

Mean facial skin surface pH according to skin phototype, age group, and geographic location
title: Facial Skin Diversity: A Pooled Analysis of Brazilian Studies

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the effects of two Mat Pilates exercise programs on musculoskeletal symptoms and body composition in women with overweight or obesity.

A total of 90 women will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will complete the same 36 supervised Mat Pilates sessions, each lasting approximately 60 minutes. One group will exercise three times per week for 12 weeks, while the other will exercise twice per week for 18 weeks.

Musculoskeletal symptoms and body composition will be assessed before and after the exercise programs. The main outcome will be the number of body regions in which participants report pain or discomfort during the previous four weeks. Changes in body weight, body fat, muscle mass, and other body composition measurements will also be examined.

The study will investigate whether completing the same amount of Mat Pilates exercise over different periods leads to different health outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Number of Anatomical Regions With Musculoskeletal Symptoms in the Previous Four Weeks
title: Comparing 12-Week and 18-Week Mat Pilates Programs in Women With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary:
Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a serious condition in which the immune system becomes overactive and causes widespread inflammation. This study will evaluate firsekibart, a long-acting medicine that blocks interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), in adults with refractory HLH patients.

The study will assess whether firsekibart can help control inflammation during the first 4 weeks of treatment and will monitor side effects. The results may help researchers understand the potential benefits and risks of firsekibart for patients with HLH.
primary_outcomes: Overall response rate (CR+PR+CI) at Day 14

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether wearable devices can accurately monitor health changes in adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and iron deficiency. The study will also evaluate how and when intravenous (IV) iron improves exercise capacity, sleep, stress, and other health measures in this population. The main questions it aims to answer are:

How does IV iron affect exercise performance measured by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET)? How accurate are lab-built wearable devices compared with standard CPET equipment? Can commercial wearable devices such as the Apple Watch and Oura Ring reliably monitor heart rate, oxygen levels, activity, sleep, and stress over time in people with HFrEF and iron deficiency?

Researchers will compare participants who receive IV iron at the start of the study with participants who receive IV iron after the final study visit to see how iron treatment changes exercise capacity and wearable device measurements.

Participants will:

* Wear an Apple Watch and Oura Ring for about 120 days during regular life
* Complete 2 CPET tests approximately 90 days apart
* Wear additional investigational lab-built monitoring devices during CPET visits
* Complete brief weekly questionnaires and daily smartwatch electrocardiograms (ECGs)
* Receive IV iron either at the first CPET visit or after the second CPET visit depending on study group assignment
