brief_summary:
Pregnant women with threatened preterm labor may experience increased anxiety and stress during hospitalization. Virtual reality (VR) may provide a non-pharmacological approach to help reduce these psychological symptoms by creating an immersive and relaxing environment.

This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of viewing videos featuring nature images and natural environmental sounds through VR headsets on anxiety, stress, and physiological parameters in pregnant women with threatened preterm labor. Participants will be randomly assigned to either the VR intervention group or the control group. Women in the intervention group will view nature-based videos with natural environmental sounds using a VR headset, while women in the control group will receive routine care.

The study will assess anxiety and stress levels, salivary cortisol levels, and physiological parameters, including heart rate, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation. The findings will help determine whether a nature-based VR intervention can be used as a supportive non-pharmacological approach for pregnant women hospitalized with threatened preterm labor.
primary_outcomes: Change in Anxiety Level Assessed by the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21)
Change in Pregnancy-Specific Stress Assessed by the Pregnancy Stress Assessment Scale
Change in Salivary Cortisol Level
title: Effects of Virtual Reality Nature Videos on Anxiety, Stress, and Physiological Parameters in Pregnant Women With Threatened Preterm Labor

brief_summary:
Background People with rectal cancer often receive chemotherapy and radiation before surgery to shrink the tumor. For patients whose tumor shrinks a lot (at least 50% in size) but who still need an operation, the standard surgery is total mesorectal excision (TME) - removing the rectum and a large amount of surrounding tissue. This extensive operation can cause problems such as leakage where the bowel is reconnected and changes in bowel/anal function. TME-short surgery is a newer, less extensive operation: it removes a shorter segment of the rectum and its covering tissue but keeps the same margin of healthy tissue around the tumor. The aim is to preserve more bowel and better blood supply, thereby reducing leakage and protecting bowel function, while still removing the cancer safely.

Purpose This study tests whether TME-short surgery is as effective as standard TME surgery for controlling cancer (a "non-inferiority" test), and whether it lowers the risk of surgical complications and better preserves bowel function.

Who can join Adults aged 18-79 with mid-to-low rectal cancer (tumor no more than 10 cm from the anal verge) whose tumor shrank at least 50% after neoadjuvant therapy but who still need surgery and are not suitable for a "watch-and-wait" approach. People are not eligible if the cancer has spread, expected survival is under 6 months, age is 80 or older, or they cannot undergo surgery.

What participants will do After giving consent and confirming eligibility, participants are randomly assigned (like a coin toss, 1:1) to either TME-short surgery or standard TME surgery. Both groups receive the same pre- and post-surgery care, the same pathology review, and the same follow-up plan. Because the two operations look different, neither participants nor surgeons can be blinded to the type (open-label); however, an independent committee, kept unaware of group assignment, will review the main cancer outcomes. Follow-up visits take place at 30 days, 90 days, 6 months, and 12 months after surgery, then every 6 months up to 3 years, and once a year up to 5 years.

Main measures The primary outcome is the percentage of participants alive and free of cancer recurrence 3 years after surgery (3-year disease-free survival). Secondary outcomes include surgical leakage within 30 days, bowel/anal function (LARS score), 2- and 5-year survival, local recurrence, distant spread, and overall survival.

Study size and timing About 606 participants across multiple hospitals; enrollment runs from October 2026 to October 2029, with follow-up continuing to 5 years after the last surgery.
primary_outcomes: 3-year Disease-Free Survival (DFS) Rate
title: Efficacy and Safety of TME-short Surgery for Rectal Cancer After Neoadjuvant Therapy

brief_summary:
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a common mental disorder with intrusive unwanted thoughts and repetitive compulsions that severely disrupt daily function and quality of life. First-line treatments include antidepressants and cognitive-behavioral therapy. Many patients retain residual symptoms or fail to respond adequately. Medications may cause gastrointestinal or sexual side effects, while psychotherapy requires long courses and has limited accessibility.

Non-invasive neuromodulation, including rTMS, tDCS and neurofeedback, serves as a promising adjunctive therapy for OCD. These techniques non-surgically modulate brain activity without anesthesia. Modalities differ in symptom relief, onset speed, adverse risks, cost, duration and access. Patient preferences affect treatment adherence and clinical decisions, yet few studies quantify OCD patients' preferences for these interventions.

This multicenter questionnaire study adopts a Discrete Choice Experiment (DCE). Participants complete hypothetical treatment-choice surveys; no real clinical intervention is provided. Semi-structured interviews with 10 OCD patients and 10 psychiatrists defined six core attributes: symptom improvement, time to relief, adverse risk, total cost, full-course duration and treatment location.

Each choice set offers two virtual treatment plans plus an opt-out option. All choice tasks are divided into 3 parallel questionnaire versions (14 choice sets per version) to reduce respondent burden. The survey collects demographics, OCI-R scores and validity check items.

A pilot test with 30 OCD patients at Shanghai Mental Health Center optimizes the questionnaire. The formal phase targets 1200 valid responses across four sites. Eligible participants are psychiatrist-diagnosed OCD patients able to complete surveys independently, with no age/gender limits. Surveys are available online or on-site. Careless responses will be excluded. Participation is voluntary; participants may withdraw anytime without impact on routine care.

This study quantifies how treatment features shape patients' decisions, identifies priority factors, and explores preference heterogeneity across patient subgroups. Results will inform patient-centered care and group standards for OCD neuromodulation. Only aggregated statistical data will be published; no identifiable individual data will be disclosed.

Study risks are minimal. Respondents may experience temporary negative mood. Strict de-identification and encryption protect privacy. Support is available for emotional distress or data security events. The study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Shanghai Mental Health Center.

The survey takes 20-30 minutes. No free neuromodulation treatment or medical advice is provided.
primary_outcomes: Preference coefficients of patients for neuromodulation attributes
title: Patient Preferences for Non-Invasive Neuromodulation Interventions Among Individuals With Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Discrete Choice Experiment

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether robotic surgery for an inguinal hernia can be carried out using remote control between Aabenraa, Denmark, and Nuuk, Greenland. An inguinal hernia is a bulge in the groin caused by tissue pushing through a weak area in the abdominal wall.

The patient, robot and local operating team will be at Queen Ingrid's Hospital in Nuuk. A surgeon at Hospital of Southern Jutland in Aabenraa will control the robotic instruments through a communication link. A local surgeon will remain scrubbed beside the patient throughout the remote part of the operation, ready to take over immediately if needed. The operation can then be completed locally using robotic, conventional keyhole or open surgery.

Up to two adults living in Greenland with an uncomplicated inguinal hernia on one side may participate. If the first remote procedure is completed as planned, the project will end after one participant. A second attempt may take place only if technical problems prevent the first remote procedure from being completed as planned without endangering the patient, and after a documented review.

The researchers will record whether the remote procedure can be completed, the quality of the connection, any need for local takeover, and surgical outcomes through 30 days. Patients will be asked about pain, satisfaction, perceived safety and their experience of information and consent. The operating team will evaluate communication, working arrangements and preparation.

The findings will help identify practical requirements for future remote surgical support in Greenland. This small study will not establish whether remote surgery is safer or more effective than surgery performed entirely by a local surgeon.
interventions: Toumai Robotic Surgical System for Remote Inguinal Hernia Repair
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Successful Setup of the Toumai Remote-Control Function
Number of Participants Whose Planned Remote Phase Was Completed Using Toumai Remote Instrument Control
title: Robotic Telesurgery Between Aabenraa and Nuuk for Inguinal Hernia Repair

This study examines how reduced kidney function affects the amount of SAL0140 in the blood and how the drug is removed from the body after a single oral dose. It also evaluates the safety of SAL0140 in adults with kidney impairment and in matched healthy adults with normal kidney function.

Part A includes adults with mild or moderate kidney impairment and matched healthy adults. Part B, if conducted based on the results of Part A, includes adults with severe kidney impairment and a separate matched healthy group. All participants receive a single 10 mg dose of SAL0140 tablets. Blood and urine samples are collected through 168 hours after dosing.
primary_outcomes: Cmax
AUC0-last
AUC0-inf
title: A Study to Evaluate the Pharmacokinetics of SAL0140 Tablets in Participants With Varying Degrees of Renal Impairment and Matched Healthy Participants With Normal Renal Function

brief_summary: Menopause is a natural part of aging that affects most women during midlife. Symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, sleep disruption, and mood changes are common, yet many women do not receive adequate education or care to manage them. This study is developing WHIM (Women's Health in Menopause), an online platform that allows menopausal women to participate in group medical visits and access menopause education from home. To make sure the platform meets the needs of real patients and providers, this study gathers feedback through interviews and usability sessions. Participants are not assigned to any treatment. Instead, they share their perspectives on the platform's design and ease of use.
primary_outcomes: System Usability Scale (SUS)
title: WHIM (Women's Health in Menopause): Promoting Healthy Aging in Menopausal Women

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether drinking FaOH- and FaDOH-rich carrot juice may improve disease activity in people with chronic pouchitis. The study will also assess whether the carrot juice is safe and tolerable. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does drinking 100 mL of carrot juice daily for eight weeks improve pouchitis disease activity, as assessed by pouchoscopy and stool samples?
* Is the carrot juice safe and tolerable, and can participants follow the treatment?

Participants will:

* Drink 100 mL of carrot juice daily for eight weeks.
* Have a pouchoscopy and provide a stool sample at baseline and week 8.
* Complete questionnaires and keep a diary of their daily carrot juice intake.
* Take part in follow-up conversations at week 4, week 8, and day 90.
primary_outcomes: Change in chronic pouchitis disease activity measured by the modified Pouchitis Disease Activity Index (mPDAI) total score from baseline to week 8
title: A Clinical Feasibility Study of Falcarinol- and Falcarindiol-Rich Carrot Juice as Treatment for Chronic Pouchitis
